definition_zh: 偏瘫；半身不遂
definition_en: paralysis of the muscles on one side of the body, usually caused by damage to the brain on the opposite side
core_image: 中风之后，身体被一条无形的中线切成两半，左臂和左腿都抬不起来
scene: 病房里，物理治疗师扶着一位中风老人练习站立。Hemiplegia left him unable to lift his left arm.
sceneCN: 这里 hemiplegia 是「偏瘫」（第 1 个义项：身体一侧的肌肉瘫痪）；句意：偏瘫使他抬不起左臂。

forms.label: 不可数名词（通常无复数）

derivatives.zh: 偏瘫的；偏瘫患者
轻偏瘫；一侧肢体轻度无力
轻偏瘫的
截瘫；下半身瘫痪

senses.title: Paralysis of one side of the body
senses.definition: a loss of muscle function affecting the arm, leg, and often the face on a single side of the body
senses.definitionCN: 一侧的手臂、腿、往往还有面部失去运动能力的状况
senses.example: Hemiplegia after a stroke usually affects the side opposite the brain injury.
senses.exampleCN: 中风后的偏瘫通常影响脑损伤的对侧身体。
senses.why: The Greek prefix hemi- means half and -plegia means a stroke or blow, so the word pictures a body struck on half its frame.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语前缀 hemi- 意为「一半」，-plegia 意为「击打」，所以这个词画出的是身体半边被击中、半边失能的画面。

senses.title: The side that no longer answers
senses.definition: the affected half of a patient body, spoken of as a single working unit in clinical notes
senses.definitionCN: 患者身上受影响的那一半，病历中常把它当作一个整体来谈论
senses.example: Nurses check the hemiplegia every hour for pressure sores.
senses.exampleCN: 护士每小时检查患侧，以防压疮。
senses.why: Once the half-body is named, clinicians can treat it as a place to inspect, pad, and position, so the disease name shifts to the part it marks.
senses.whyCN: 一旦半边身体有了名目，医护人员就能把它当作位置去检查、垫护与摆放，病名于是指向它标记的那一侧身体。

senses.title: A one-sidedness in movement
senses.titleCN: 单侧运动障碍；半侧失灵
senses.definition: a general quality of movement controlled by one side while the other side stays still or stiff
senses.definitionCN: 活动由身体一侧主导、另一侧僵硬或不参与的一般特性
senses.example: Observers noted a hemiplegia in the way she always led with her right shoulder.
senses.exampleCN: 旁人注意到她总用右肩带头，带着一种半侧失灵的姿态。
senses.why: Because the noun names one half doing what two halves should do, writers borrow it for any lopsided habit of motion.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个词本指本该两侧分担、却只有一半在动，写作者便借用它来形容任何歪向一侧的动作习惯。

senses.title: A one-sided paralysis of a group
senses.definition: figurative use for an organisation, team, or plan that can act on only one side and stalls on the other
senses.definitionCN: 比喻性用法，指组织、团队或计划只能作用于一侧，另一侧陷入停顿
senses.example: With the ports closed, the regional economy suffered a kind of hemiplegia.
senses.exampleCN: 港口关闭后，该地区经济陷入了某种半边瘫痪。
senses.why: The body picture offers itself to any system that needs two working sides to move, which is how the medical noun enters journalism.
senses.whyCN: 身体图景天然适合任何需要两侧同时发力才能运转的系统，医学名词正是这样进入新闻报道的。

intro.en: Hemiplegia joins the Greek prefix hemi-, meaning half, to -plegia, a stroke or blow, so the word names a half body that has been struck.
intro.cn: hemiplegia 由希腊语前缀 hemi-（一半）与 -plegia（击打）合成，所命名的是被「击中」了一半的身体。

items.en: A root reconstructed as semi- carries the meaning one and the same, later the sense of half.
items.cn: 一般认为可重构出词根 semi-，意为「同一」，后来发展出「一半」之义。

items.en: Hemi means half, and plessein means to strike.
items.cn: 希腊语 hemi 意为一半，plessein 意为击打。

items.en: Plegia means a blow or a stroke, the sudden affliction of a body.
items.cn: plegia 意为击打或中风，即身体突然遭受的侵袭。

items.en: Medical Latin combines hemi- and -plegia for paralysis of half the body, written in Greek letters at first.
items.cn: 十七世纪的医学拉丁语以 hemi- 与 -plegia 合成偏瘫之名，最初直接写作希腊字母。

items.en: The word enters English medical writing as the learned term for one-sided palsy.
items.cn: 十七世纪该词进入英语医学文体，成为单侧瘫痪的学术名称。

items.en: Modern usage separates hemiplegia from hemiparesis and anchors the cause in the opposite hemisphere.
items.cn: 现代用法把偏瘫与轻偏瘫区分开，并把病因定位在对侧大脑半球。

note.en: The first group collects words built with the half prefix or the paralysis ending; the second collects other names for lost or weakened movement.
note.cn: 第一组收集由「一半」前缀或「瘫痪」词尾构成的词；第二组收集其他表示失去或减弱运动能力的词。

entries.definition: One of the two halves of the brain, each controlling the body side opposite to it.
entries.definitionCN: 大脑的两个半球之一，各管身体的对侧。

entries.definition: Weakness rather than full paralysis on one side, the milder neighbour of this word.
entries.definitionCN: 一侧无力而非完全瘫痪，是本词的较轻版本。

entries.definition: Loss of movement in the legs and lower body, from para- beside rather than hemi- half.
entries.definitionCN: 双腿与下半身失去运动能力，前缀是 para-「旁侧」而非 hemi-。

entries.definition: The ending used in medical compounds for a stroke or paralysis.
entries.definitionCN: 医学复合词中表示中风或瘫痪的词尾。

entries.definition: Loss of voluntary movement in any part of the body, not necessarily one side.
entries.definitionCN: 身体任一部分丧失随意运动，不限于一侧。

entries.definition: The old everyday name for paralysis, now mainly in fixed expressions.
entries.definitionCN: 瘫痪的旧称，如今多用于固定说法中。

entries.definition: A sudden loss of blood supply to the brain, the most frequent cause of this condition.
entries.definitionCN: 脑部突然供血不足，是本症最常见的成因。

entries.definition: Paralysis confined to a single limb rather than a whole side.
entries.definitionCN: 瘫痪只限一个肢体，而非整侧身体。

normalIntro.en: Hemiplegia is half plus stroke: hemi- names the side, and -plegia is the blow that took the movement away.
normalIntro.cn: hemiplegia 就是「一半」加「击打」：hemi- 指明哪一侧，-plegia 是夺走运动能力的那一击。

normal.en: Hemi- marks half in many medical nouns, as in hemisphere.
normal.cn: hemi- 在 hemisphere 等许多医学名词中都表示一半。

normal.en: The ending -plegia means paralysis, so every word with it names a body part that will not move.
normal.cn: 词尾 -plegia 意为瘫痪，凡带此词尾的词都指某个不能活动的身体部位。

normal.en: Hemiplegia is the noun, while hemiplegic works as adjective and as a name for the patient.
normal.cn: hemiplegia 是名词，hemiplegic 可作形容词，也可指患者。

normal.en: Trust the opposite rule: damage to one brain side shows up on the other body side.
normal.cn: 记住对侧规律：一侧脑损伤会表现在身体的另一侧。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with paraplegia, which takes the legs rather than one side.
normal.cn: 不要和 paraplegia 混淆，后者瘫痪的是双腿而非一侧。

abstract.en: Picture a straight line drawn down the centre of a body, with one half refusing to cross it.
abstract.cn: 想象从身体正中画下一条直线，有一半身体拒绝越线。

abstract.en: Imagine a puppet whose strings on one side have been cut.
abstract.cn: 想象一只木偶，一侧的提线全被剪断。

abstract.en: Think of a clock that runs on two hands, with one stuck at the same minute.
abstract.cn: 想象一座靠两只指针行走的钟，一只指针卡在同一分钟。

examples.en: The boy was born with spastic hemiplegia on his right side.
examples.cn: 这个男孩天生右侧痉挛性偏瘫。

examples.en: After the stroke she was treated for hemiplegia and had to relearn walking.
examples.cn: 中风后她因偏瘫接受治疗，不得不重新学走路。

examples.en: Physiotherapists train hemiplegic patients to use the affected half again.
examples.cn: 物理治疗师训练偏瘫患者重新使用患侧身体。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「黑米扑倒鸡」——黑米一撒，半边身子扑过去把鸡按倒，只剩一半能使劲，所以 hemiplegia 是偏瘫；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 hemi-（一半）＋ -plegia（击打、中风）→ 医学拉丁语 hemiplegia（半边身体受创）→ 英语 hemiplegia，核心义「身体被击瘫了一半」。

sensesIntro.en: The noun begins as the medical diagnosis of one-sided paralysis, extends to the affected side itself, then loosens into lopsided motion and finally into any system half stuck.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词先指单侧瘫痪的医学诊断，再指患侧身体本身，之后放宽为偏离中线的动作，最后比喻任何半边停摆的系统。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body split by an invisible centre line, one half still moving and the other hanging loose.
core.cn: 核心意象：身体被一条看不见的中线分开，一半仍在动，另一半松垮垂下。

branches.en: The diagnosis of one-sided paralysis is the organising sense.
branches.cn: 单侧瘫痪的诊断是组织性义项。

branches.en: Clinical notes turn the condition into a place to inspect.
branches.cn: 临床记录把病症转化为可检查的部位。

branches.en: The lopsided manner of moving keeps the body picture while dropping the clinic.
branches.cn: 歪向一侧的动作方式保留身体图景而离开诊室。

branches.en: Journalism transfers the half body to economies and institutions.
branches.cn: 新闻写作把「半边身体」迁移到经济与机构上。

branches.en: All three keep the idea of one working half and one dead half.
branches.cn: 三者都保留着「一半能动、一半不能动」的观念。

intro.en: The word is a Greek prefix plus a Greek noun ending, and the whole family about half-body and full-body loss grows from those two pieces.
intro.cn: 这个词由希腊语前缀与希腊语名词词尾拼成，围绕「半身」与「全身」的整个词族都从这两块构件长出来。

latinIntro.en: Greek hemi- and -plegia pass into medical Latin unchanged, and Latin supplies the equivalent root for half, semi-.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 hemi- 与 -plegia 原样进入医学拉丁语，拉丁语另有表「一半」的同义词根 semi-。

items.example: Hemi- fixes the size at one half of the body.
items.exampleCN: hemi- 把范围限定为身体的一半。

items.example: The ending names the loss of movement.
items.exampleCN: 该词尾点明运动能力的丧失。

items.example: The strike image sits inside the ending.
items.exampleCN: 「击打」的意象藏在词尾之中。

items.meaning: half of a sphere, especially half the brain
items.example: The injured hemisphere controls the opposite half.
items.exampleCN: 受损的半球控制身体的对侧。

items.example: Paresis marks weakness where plegia marks loss.
items.exampleCN: paresis 表无力，plegia 表完全丧失。

items.example: Hemiparesis is the milder cousin of the full term.
items.exampleCN: 轻偏瘫是偏瘫一词的较轻近亲。

items.example: Para- replaces half when both legs are taken.
items.exampleCN: 双腿皆瘫时，para- 取代了表「一半」的前缀。

items.example: Paraplegia and hemiplegia share the closing ending.
items.exampleCN: 截瘫与偏瘫共享相同的词尾。

items.meaning: of one-sided paralysis; a patient with it
items.example: The -ic form modifies gait and patient.
items.exampleCN: -ic 形式可修饰步态与患者。

items.example: The suffix turns the condition into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 该词尾把病症转成形容词。

definition_zh: 肝炎；肝脏炎症
definition_en: inflammation of the liver, usually caused by a virus but sometimes by alcohol, drugs, or the body attacking itself
core_image: 肝脏本该柔软温润，发炎后却肿得紧绷发烫，轻微一按就疼
scene: 校医院门口贴着一张提示，提醒新生接种疫苗。Hepatitis B spreads through contact with infected blood.
sceneCN: 这里 hepatitis 是「肝炎」（第 1 个义项：肝脏的炎症）；句意：乙型肝炎经由接触受感染的血液传播。

forms.label: 不可数名词（无普通复数）

derivatives.zh: 肝炎的；患肝炎的
肝病学
肝病专科医师
肝细胞
有肝毒性的；损肝的

senses.title: Inflammation of the liver
senses.definition: swelling and irritation of liver tissue that may come from a virus, alcohol, a drug, or the immune system
senses.definitionCN: 肝组织肿胀发炎，可源于病毒、酒精、药物或身体自我攻击
senses.example: Acute hepatitis can start with nausea, fever, and yellowing of the eyes.
senses.exampleCN: 急性肝炎可先出现恶心、发热和眼白发黄。
senses.why: The Greek stem hepat- means liver and the ending -itis means inflammation, so the word simply names which organ is inflamed.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语词干 hepat- 意为「肝」，词尾 -itis 意为「炎症」，所以这个词就是点名哪个器官发了炎。

senses.title: A named virus of the liver
senses.definition: the short clinical name for one of the liver viruses, written with a letter such as A, B, or C
senses.definitionCN: 对某一种嗜肝病毒的简称，常以字母标明类型
senses.example: Doctors screened every new donor for hepatitis C.
senses.exampleCN: 医生对每一位新献血者都做了丙型肝炎筛查。
senses.why: Because the viruses are labelled by the disease they cause, the noun itself became the shorthand name for each strain.
senses.whyCN: 因为这类病毒按所致疾病命名，这个词本身便成了各型病毒的简称。

senses.title: A long-running liver disease
senses.definition: the persistent disease that the liver viruses leave behind, often silent for years and sometimes scarring the liver
senses.definitionCN: 嗜肝病毒留下的长期病症，常多年无症状，有时会导致肝纤维化
senses.example: Untreated chronic hepatitis may slowly turn into cirrhosis.
senses.exampleCN: 未经治疗的慢性肝炎可能慢慢演变为肝硬化。
senses.why: The acute swelling can settle into years of quiet damage, so speakers use the same noun for the slow disease rather than the flare.
senses.whyCN: 急性的肿痛可以沉淀成多年悄无声息的损伤，于是人们用同一个名词指慢病，而不只是指发作。

senses.title: Loose talk for a liver complaint
senses.definition: informal reference to a liver problem in general, often used by patients who have no exact diagnosis
senses.definitionCN: 口语中对肝脏问题的一般说法，常为尚未明确诊断的患者所用
senses.example: The old sailor blamed the climate for his hepatitis.
senses.exampleCN: 那位老水手把肝病归咎于当地气候。
senses.why: Where the clinical word is unknown, lay speakers borrow it as a broad label for any aching liver.
senses.whyCN: 在不知道专业说法时，普通人便借这个词笼统指一切肝部不适。

intro.en: Hepatitis pairs the Greek stem hepat-, liver, with the medical Latin ending -itis, inflammation, so the word means the inflamed liver.
intro.cn: hepatitis 把希腊语词干 hepat-（肝）与医学拉丁语词尾 -itis（炎症）配在一起，意思就是「发炎的肝」。

items.en: A reconstructed root yekwr for liver leaves descendants in Greek, Latin, and English.
items.cn: 一般认为可重构出表「肝」的词根 yekwr，其后代见于希腊语、拉丁语与英语。

items.en: Hepar is the liver, and its stem hepat- supplies medical compounds.
items.cn: 希腊语 hepar 意为肝，其词干 hepat- 用于构成医学复合词。

items.en: Latin iecur names the liver, and medical Latin takes over the suffix -itis for inflammation.
items.cn: 拉丁语 iecur 指肝，医学拉丁语则采用希腊式词尾 -itis 表示炎症。

items.en: Greek physicians already use hepatitis for a disease of the liver.
items.cn: 公元前二世纪的希腊医生已用 hepatitis 称肝脏疾病。

items.en: The medical term appears in English during the eighteenth century, and the plural hepatitides is rare but attested.
items.cn: 该医学名词在十八世纪进入英语；极少见的复数 hepatitides 亦有文献可查。

items.en: The discovery of the liver viruses from 1947 onward fixes the letters A, B, C, D, and E on the disease name.
items.cn: 自一九四七年起陆续发现嗜肝病毒，A、B、C、D、E 等字母遂固定于病名之上。

note.en: The first group collects words built on the liver stem or the inflammation ending; the second collects other words and diseases of the liver.
note.cn: 第一组收集建立在「肝」词干或「炎症」词尾上的词；第二组收集其他与肝脏相关的词与病名。

entries.definition: An enlarged liver, from the liver stem plus -megaly, enlargement.
entries.definitionCN: 肝肿大，由「肝」词干加表「增大」的 -megaly 构成。

entries.definition: The branch of medicine that studies the liver, ending in -logy, the study of.
entries.definitionCN: 研究肝脏的医学分支，词尾 -logy 意为「学科」。

entries.definition: Inflammation of the stomach lining, built with the stomach stem gastr-.
entries.definitionCN: 胃黏膜发炎，词干是表示「胃」的 gastr-。

entries.definition: A liver cell, from the liver stem plus -cyte, a cell.
entries.definitionCN: 肝细胞，由「肝」词干加表「细胞」的 -cyte 构成。

entries.definition: A tumour of the liver, from hepat- plus -oma, a growth.
entries.definitionCN: 肝脏肿瘤，由 hepat- 加表「肿块」的 -oma 构成。

entries.definition: Scarring of the liver that can follow years of hepatitis or heavy drinking.
entries.definitionCN: 肝脏结疤，可继多年肝炎或大量饮酒之后发生。

entries.definition: Yellowing of skin and eyes, a common symptom rather than a cause.
entries.definitionCN: 皮肤与眼白发黄，常见为症状而非病因。

entries.definition: The body response of heat, swelling, and pain that the ending -itis names.
entries.definitionCN: 身体发热、肿胀、疼痛的反应，正是 -itis 所表示的过程。

entries.definition: The everyday phrase for the whole family of liver disorders, including this one.
entries.definitionCN: 涵盖全部肝病的日常说法，本词也在其中。

normalIntro.en: Hepatitis is liver plus inflammation, so the word tells you at once the organ and what has gone wrong with it.
normalIntro.cn: hepatitis 就是「肝」加「炎症」，这个词一下子把器官和出事的性质都说清楚了。

normal.en: The stem hepat- belongs to liver words, from the Greek name for the organ.
normal.cn: 词干 hepat- 属于「肝」这一词族，源自希腊语对肝脏的称呼。

normal.en: The ending -itis means inflammation, as in gastritis and bronchitis.
normal.cn: 词尾 -itis 意为炎症，如 gastritis 与 bronchitis。

normal.en: Read the letter as the viral type: hepatitis A, B, C, D, and E travel by different routes.
normal.cn: 字母代表病毒类型：甲、乙、丙、丁、戊五型的传播途径各不相同。

normal.en: Use is or was with it; the noun has no ordinary plural.
normal.cn: 动词用 is 或 was，该名词没有普通复数形式。

normal.en: Keep it apart from cirrhosis, which is the scarring that the disease can leave.
normal.cn: 要和 cirrhosis 区分开，后者是本症可能留下的肝纤维化。

abstract.en: Picture a warm organ glowing red under the ribs and pressing against its neighbours.
abstract.cn: 想象肋下一团发红发热的脏器，肿胀得顶着邻近的器官。

abstract.en: Imagine a filter that slowly clogs while the tap above it keeps running.
abstract.cn: 想象一个过滤器缓缓堵塞，而上面的水龙头一直在放水。

abstract.en: Think of a fever thermometer rising quietly for weeks with no one noticing.
abstract.cn: 想想一支体温计悄无声息地升了好几周，却没人察觉。

examples.en: Vaccination now protects most children in the region from hepatitis B.
examples.cn: 如今接种疫苗使该地区多数儿童免受乙型肝炎侵害。

examples.en: Heavy drinking can cause a form of hepatitis that is not infectious.
examples.cn: 大量饮酒会引起一种不具传染性的肝炎。

examples.en: The clinic screens pregnant women for all common types of hepatitis.
examples.cn: 该诊所为孕妇筛查所有常见类型的肝炎。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喝怕太太」——怕太太的人不敢多喝，喝多了伤的是肝，所以 hepatitis 是肝炎；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 hepar（肝），词干 hepat- ＋ 希腊式医学词尾 -itis（炎症）→ 拉丁语 hepatitis（肝脏炎症）→ 英语 hepatitis，核心义「肝在发炎」。

sensesIntro.en: The noun starts as any inflamed liver, then becomes the shorthand name of each liver virus, then of the long illness those viruses leave, and finally a loose everyday label.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词先泛指任何发炎的肝，再成为各型嗜肝病毒的简称，继而指这些病毒留下的慢性病，最后成为口语里的泛称。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a warm, swollen liver pressing against the ribs, tender to the touch.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗温热肿胀的肝脏顶着肋骨，一碰就疼。

branches.en: The general inflammation is the organising sense.
branches.cn: 泛指的发炎是组织性义项。

branches.en: Naming the virus borrows the diagnosis as a label.
branches.cn: 命名病毒时把诊断名借来当作标签。

branches.en: The chronic disease stretches the swelling across years.
branches.cn: 慢性病症把发炎状态拉长到许多年。

branches.en: Lay talk flattens every liver complaint into the one term.
branches.cn: 口语把种种肝部不适都压成这一个词。

branches.en: All three still point at the same inflamed organ.
branches.cn: 三者指向的仍是同一颗发炎的肝。

intro.en: A Greek liver stem joins the inflammation ending -itis, and the -ic form hepatitic sits at the edge of the family.
intro.cn: 希腊语「肝」词干接上表炎症的词尾 -itis，词族的边缘还有形容词形式 hepatitic。

latinIntro.en: Greek gives the liver stem, and Latin medical writing gives the -itis pattern that now runs through hundreds of disease names.
latinIntro.cn: 「肝」词干来自希腊语，而 -itis 这一构词模式来自拉丁语医学书写，如今贯穿数百个病名。

items.example: Hepat- fixes the organ at once.
items.exampleCN: hepat- 立刻把病变器官定为肝。

items.example: The suffix turns any organ name into a disease.
items.exampleCN: 该词尾能把任何器官名变成病名。

items.example: The suffix forms hepatitic.
items.exampleCN: 该词尾构成 hepatitic。

items.example: Hepat- plus -cyte gives hepatocyte.
items.exampleCN: hepat- 加 -cyte 构成肝细胞。

items.example: Hepat- plus -oma names a liver growth.
items.exampleCN: hepat- 加 -oma 指肝脏肿块。

items.example: The ending forms hepatology.
items.exampleCN: 该词尾构成肝病学一词。

items.example: Hepato- plus -toxic gives hepatotoxic.
items.exampleCN: hepato- 加 -toxic 构成「损肝的」。

items.example: Gastr- plus -itis gives gastritis.
items.exampleCN: gastr- 加 -itis 构成胃炎。

items.example: The linking vowel joins hepat to logy.
items.exampleCN: 连接元音把 hepat 与 logy 连在一起。

items.example: The finished noun keeps both Greek pieces.
items.exampleCN: 最终的名词保留了希腊语的两个部件。

definition_zh: 草本植物的；药草制的；草本的
definition_en: made from or relating to herbs, especially plants used for medicine, flavouring, or fragrance
core_image: 竹篮里刚采下的薄荷与洋甘菊，叶片还带着露水，凑近一闻满手清香
scene: 山间民宿的老板娘端来一壶热茶，说方子是外婆传下的。The innkeeper brewed a herbal tea to help her guests sleep.
sceneCN: 这里 herbal 是「用药草制的」（第 1 个义项：由药草制成或与药草有关的）；句意：民宿主人煮了一壶草药茶帮助客人入睡。

pos.zh: 草本植物的；药草制的；草本的
本草书；草药志（现多作 herbals）

derivatives.zh: 药草；香草；草本植物
草本的；肉质茎的（植物学用语）
草药师；本草学家
除草剂
香草味的；多香草的

senses.title: Made from herbs, especially for medicine
senses.definition: prepared from plant parts that are used as remedies, teas, or tonics
senses.definitionCN: 用作物药、泡茶或当补剂的植物部位制成的
senses.example: She treats her cough with herbal syrup instead of pills.
senses.exampleCN: 她不用药片，而用草药糖浆治咳嗽。
senses.why: The Latin source herba simply means grass or green plant, and the English ending -al adds the sense of relating to, so the adjective names anything made out of such plants.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源 herba 本义就是「草、绿色草木」，英语词尾 -al 表示「与……有关」，所以这个形容词指一切由这类植物制成的东西。

senses.title: Of plants in the kitchen
senses.titleCN: 用香草调味的；香草味的
senses.definition: flavoured or scented with culinary herbs such as basil, mint, or thyme
senses.definitionCN: 用罗勒、薄荷、百里香等食用香草调味或赋香的
senses.example: The chef finished the soup with a herbal olive oil.
senses.exampleCN: 厨师最后淋上用香草浸泡的橄榄油，为汤收尾。
senses.why: The same plants move from the apothecary to the kitchen, and the adjective follows them, since herba covers any fragrant leaf used by cooks.
senses.whyCN: 同一批植物从药房走进厨房，形容词也跟着走过去，因为 herba 本就涵盖厨师所用的任何香叶。

senses.title: Botanically soft-stemmed
senses.definition: describing a plant with a soft, non-woody stem that dies back rather than forming timber
senses.definitionCN: 描述茎柔软、不成木质、会枯萎而非长成木材的植物
senses.example: The herbal layer of the forest floor is rich in ferns and wild mint.
senses.exampleCN: 森林地被的草本层长满蕨类与野薄荷。
senses.why: Because herba meant grass in the plainest sense, botanists kept that literal picture and use herbal for the soft green layer beneath the trees.
senses.whyCN: 因为 herba 最朴素的意思就是「草」，植物学家保留了这幅实景，用 herbal 指树下柔软翠绿的草本层。

senses.title: A book of plants and their uses
senses.definition: an illustrated book listing plants with their medicinal or culinary uses, a genre popular from the sixteenth century
senses.definitionCN: 罗列植物及其药用或食用价值的图文书籍，十六世纪起颇为流行
senses.example: Early herbal volumes listed which leaves would ease a fever.
senses.exampleCN: 早期的本草书会列出哪些叶子能退烧。
senses.why: The adjective was turned into a noun for the books that catalogued herbs, and that learned sense survives in the plural herbals.
senses.whyCN: 形容词被借来作名词，指收录药草的书籍，这一学术义项至今保存在复数形式 herbals 中。

senses.title: Green and plant-scented
senses.definition: tasting or smelling of fresh green plants, as in wines and oils described by tasters
senses.definitionCN: 尝起来或闻起来有新鲜青草气息的，如品鉴者所描述的葡萄酒与油
senses.example: The young white wine has a herbal note that softens with age.
senses.exampleCN: 这支年轻的白葡萄酒带有一股青草气息，随年份变得柔和。
senses.why: Tasting notes borrow the plant word to name a smell, treating grassiness as a flavour rather than a material.
senses.whyCN: 品鉴术语借用这个植物词来命名气味，把青草味当作一种风味，而非物质本身。

intro.en: Herbal is the Latin noun herba, a green plant or grass, dressed with the English ending -al that means relating to.
intro.cn: herbal 是拉丁语名词 herba（绿色草木、草）加上英语词尾 -al（与……有关的）而成。

items.en: The Latin word is usually traced to a root meaning to grow or to be green, though the reconstruction is debated.
items.cn: 一般认为拉丁语 herba 可追溯到一个表「生长、发绿」的词根，但该重构形式仍有争议。

items.en: Herba means grass, a green blade, and by extension any useful plant.
items.cn: herba 意为草、草叶，引申为任何有用的植物。

items.en: The adjective herbalis and the neuter plural herbalia appear in late Latin for things of herbs.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语出现形容词 herbalis 与中性复数 herbalia，指与草木有关之物。

items.en: French herbe keeps the plant sense and the h stayed silent in later English borrowing.
items.cn: 法语 herbe 保留植物之义，英语移植后词首的 h 又渐渐不发音。

items.en: The noun herbal is applied to printed books of plants, a booming genre of the period.
items.cn: 十六世纪名词 herbal 被用来指印刷的植物图册，是当时风行一时的书种。

items.en: The adjective widens to tea, medicine, supplements, and tasting notes, while the book sense retreats to herbals.
items.cn: 形容词扩展至茶、药、补充剂与品鉴评语，而书籍义项则退居为复数形式 herbals。

note.en: The first group collects other words built on the Latin plant stem; the second collects words about health products and plant families.
note.cn: 第一组收集建立在拉丁语植物词干上的其他词；第二组收集与保健品及植物类别相关的词。

entries.definition: A plant valued for its flavour or medicinal use; the adjective is built on it.
entries.definitionCN: 因风味或药用价值而受重视的植物，本形容词即建于其上。

entries.definition: Soft-stemmed and non-woody, the botanical adjective for plants of this kind.
entries.definitionCN: 茎柔软非木质的，是植物学中描述此类植物的形容词。

entries.definition: A person who grows or prescribes herbs, built with the ending -ist.
entries.definitionCN: 栽培或开具草药的人，由 -ist 词尾构成。

entries.definition: A chemical that kills plants, from herb plus -cide, a killing.
entries.definitionCN: 杀死植物的化学品，由 herb 加表「杀」的 -cide 构成。

entries.definition: A collection of dried plants kept for study, a place rather than a use.
entries.definitionCN: 为研究而保存的压制植物标本集，指场所而非用途。

entries.definition: Of plants in general, whether or not they are used for medicine.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指与植物有关的，不论是否供药用。

entries.definition: Having healing properties, a description of effect rather than origin.
entries.definitionCN: 具有治疗作用，描述的是效果而非来源。

entries.definition: Not made by people, a broad label often used on product packaging.
entries.definitionCN: 非人工制造的，常用于产品包装上的宽泛标签。

entries.definition: Strongly scented, the quality that makes many herbs attractive.
entries.definitionCN: 气味浓烈，正是许多药草吸引人的特质。

normalIntro.en: Herbal is a plant word with a relating-to ending, so it answers the question what is this thing made of or about.
normalIntro.cn: herbal 是一个植物词加上表「与……有关」的词尾，回答的是「这东西由什么做成或关于什么」。

normal.en: The base noun is herb, and the ending -al makes an adjective of it.
normal.cn: 基础名词是 herb，词尾 -al 将其变为形容词。

normal.en: The h is silent in English, so it sounds like erbal, but the spelling keeps the h.
normal.cn: 英语中词首的 h 不发音，读来近似 erbal，但拼写仍保留 h。

normal.en: The noun herbalist keeps the herbal shape and adds the person ending -ist.
normal.cn: 名词 herbalist 保留 herbal 的形状，再加表示人的词尾 -ist。

normal.en: Use the plural herbals only for books about plants.
normal.cn: 复数 herbals 只用于指植物类书籍。

normal.en: Pair it with tea, medicine, remedy, and garden far more than with forest or lawn.
normal.cn: 它多与 tea、medicine、remedy、garden 搭配，很少与 forest 或 lawn 连用。

abstract.en: Picture a steam curling off a cup of mint tea on a rainy afternoon.
abstract.cn: 想象雨后的下午，一杯薄荷茶上袅袅升起的热气。

abstract.en: Imagine a herbarium shelf of pressed green leaves with handwritten names.
abstract.cn: 想象一排压制的绿叶标本，旁边写着潦草的名字。

abstract.en: Think of a mortar on a wooden bench, grinding leaves into a green paste.
abstract.cn: 想想木凳上的一只研钵，把叶子捣成青绿的膏。

examples.en: Many herbal remedies have not been tested in large clinical trials.
examples.cn: 许多草药疗法尚未经过大型临床试验。

examples.en: In the Middle Ages many households relied on herbal knowledge to treat fever.
examples.cn: 在中世纪，许多家庭靠草药知识来治发烧。

examples.en: The market sells herbal oils, dried roots, and fresh herbs side by side.
examples.cn: 集市上草药油、干根与新鲜香草并排出售。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喝不」——喝不惯西药，就熬一把草叶子，所以 herbal 是草本的、草药制的；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 herba（草、绿色草木）＋ 形容词词尾 -alis / 英语 -al（与……有关的）→ herbal，核心义「与草木有关的、用草做成的」。

sensesIntro.en: The adjective starts with plants turned into remedies, moves to kitchen flavouring, keeps the botanical sense of soft green growth, and lends itself to books of plants and to tasting notes.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个形容词从「做成药的植物」出发，转到厨房调味与植物学的「软茎草本」，再借给记录植物的书籍与品鉴评语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bundle of fresh green leaves picked for a purpose, from medicine to a cup of tea.
core.cn: 核心意象：一束带着露水的新鲜绿叶，被采下来派上用途，从药材到一杯茶。

branches.en: Plants turned into remedies organise the word.
branches.cn: 做成药的植物是这个词的组织性义项。

branches.en: Culinary herbs keep the fragrant leaf and drop the cure.
branches.cn: 食用香草保留了香叶、舍去了疗效。

branches.en: Botany keeps the plainest sense of grass and soft stems.
branches.cn: 植物学保留了「草」与软茎的最朴素含义。

branches.en: Printed plant books and tasting notes turn the plant into a reference and a smell.
branches.cn: 植物图册与品鉴评语把植物变成参考资料与一种气味。

branches.en: All three rest on the same green leaf, used in three different rooms.
branches.cn: 三者都立足于同一片绿叶，只是用在三间不同的房间里。

intro.en: The family grows from the Latin plant stem herba, and the endings -al, -aceous, -ist, -ium, and -cide branch out from it.
intro.cn: 这个家族从拉丁语植物词干 herba 长出，再由 -al、-aceous、-ist、-ium、-cide 等词尾分出枝杈。

latinIntro.en: Latin herba is a green plant or grass, and the related adjective herbalis feeds the English ending -al.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 herba 意为绿色植物或草，其相关形容词 herbalis 为英语词尾 -al 提供了形态依据。

items.example: Herba is the plant stem of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: herba 是整个词族的植物词干。

items.example: The Latin adjective supplies the -al shape.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语形容词提供 -al 这一形态。

items.example: Herb plus -al becomes herbal.
items.exampleCN: herb 加 -al 构成 herbal。

items.example: The suffix forms herbaceous, meaning soft-stemmed.
items.exampleCN: 该词尾构成 herbaceous，意为草本的。

items.meaning: a person who does or studies
items.example: The suffix -ist marks a person who works with herbs.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ist 标示以草药为业之人。

items.example: The ending helps build herbarium.
items.exampleCN: 该词尾参与构成 herbarium。

items.example: Herb plus -cide gives herbicide.
items.exampleCN: herb 加 -cide 构成除草剂。

items.meaning: a plant used for flavour or medicine
items.meaningCN: 供调味或药用的草本植物
items.example: Herb is the base form without the ending.
items.exampleCN: herb 是不带词尾的基础形式。

items.meaning: a person who works with herbs
items.example: The person noun adds -ist to the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 表示人的名词在形容词后加 -ist。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of
items.example: Herb plus -y gives herby, another smell adjective.
items.exampleCN: herb 加 -y 构成 herby，是另一个气味形容词。

definition_zh: 除草剂；杀草药
definition_en: a chemical substance used to kill unwanted plants, especially weeds in fields and gardens
core_image: 喷雾器压低喷头，一道细雾落在杂草上，叶尖先卷曲，随后整片枯黄
scene: 田埂上的杂草长得比庄稼还高，农场主背起药桶，沿着垄沟慢慢往前走。The farmer sprayed herbicide along the rows to clear the weeds.
sceneCN: 这里 herbicide 是「除草剂」（第 1 个义项：用来杀死杂草的化学药剂）；句意：农场主沿着一行行垄沟喷洒除草剂，清除杂草。

collocations.zh: 抗除草剂性；除草剂抗性

derivatives.zh: herbicide 去掉词尾 e 加 -al 构成，义为「除草的；杀草的」
herbicide 的前半部分，义为「草本植物；草药」
与 herbicide 同用 -cide 词尾构成，义为「杀虫剂」，是上位概念的同类词
与 herbicide 同用 -cide 词尾构成，义为「杀虫剂」，专指对付昆虫的药剂

senses.title: A weed-killing chemical
senses.definition: a chemical substance used to destroy or stop the growth of unwanted plants such as weeds
senses.definitionCN: 用来杀死杂草或阻止杂草生长的化学物质
senses.example: The farmer sprayed herbicide along the rows to clear the weeds.
senses.exampleCN: 农场主沿着一行行垄沟喷洒除草剂，清除杂草。
senses.why: The second half of the word is the Latin verb caedere, to cut down, so a herbicide is literally a plant-cutter in liquid form.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的后半部分是拉丁语动词 caedere（砍倒、杀死），所以除草剂字面上就是「液态的割草者」。

senses.title: One of a class of crop chemicals
senses.definition: the class name for weed-control products, usually listed beside insecticides and fungicides
senses.definitionCN: 一类控制杂草的药剂名称，常与杀虫剂、杀菌剂并列出现
senses.example: Modern farms use a wide range of herbicides on cereal crops.
senses.exampleCN: 现代农场在谷物作物上使用多种除草剂。
senses.why: The -cide ending has become a productive academic label, so the word often names a whole group rather than one bottle.
senses.whyCN: -cide 词尾已经成为能产的学术标签，因此这个词也常指一整类产品，而不只是某一瓶药水。

senses.title: A tool in vegetation management
senses.definition: chemical weed control as a method in forestry, rail maintenance, or land restoration
senses.definitionCN: 林业、铁路维护或土地恢复中作为方法使用的化学除草手段
senses.example: Railway crews rely on herbicide to keep the tracks clear.
senses.exampleCN: 铁路工作人员依靠除草剂保持铁轨畅通。
senses.why: Once the product is trusted, the noun turns into a general method word for keeping land free of unwanted plants.
senses.whyCN: 这种产品被普遍采用之后，名词就变成一种通用方法词，表示让土地不长杂草。

senses.title: A debated public issue
senses.definition: the widespread chemical killing of plants seen as a risk to water, insects, and nearby crops
senses.definitionCN: 大规模用化学药剂杀死植物，被看作对水源、昆虫和邻近作物的风险
senses.example: Residents raised concerns about herbicide run-off into the river.
senses.exampleCN: 居民对除草剂流入河流提出了担忧。
senses.why: Anything that kills plants also stirs debate, so the word gathers an environmental and policy sense.
senses.whyCN: 凡是能杀死植物的东西都会引发争论，于是这个词又吸附了环境与政策层面的含义。

intro.en: Herbicide is a modern scientific compound made from Latin herba, a plant or herb, and the ending -cide from caedere, to cut down or kill.
intro.cn: herbicide 是现代科学造词，由拉丁语 herba（草木）与词尾 -cide 组合而成，后者来自 caedere（砍倒、杀死）。

items.en: herba meant grass, green plants, or a herb, and it also named the crop the plant grew in.
items.cn: herba 指草、绿色植物或草药，也用来表示植物长大作物的田块。

items.en: caedere meant to cut or strike down, the source of many -cide words.
items.cn: caedere 意为砍、击倒，是众多 -cide 词的来源。

items.en: Homicida and similar words already joined -cide to a Latin stem meaning whoever or whatever kills.
items.cn: 拉丁语中 homicida 一类词早已把 -cide 与词干结合，表示「杀死者」。

items.en: Herbicide is coined in English scientific writing to name a chemical that kills weeds.
items.cn: 英语科技写作中造出 herbicide 一词，用来指杀死杂草的化学药剂。

items.en: Wartime and postwar farming quickened interest in selective weed killers.
items.cn: 战时与战后农业使人们对选择性除草剂产生浓厚兴趣。

items.en: The word now sits in a family with pesticide, insecticide, and fungicide.
items.cn: 现代英语中这个词与 pesticide、insecticide、fungicide 构成同一个词族。

note.en: The first group gathers words built on the -cide ending and on herb; the second gathers chemicals used to control other living things.
note.cn: 第一组收以 -cide 构词、以及与 herb 同源的词；第二组收用来对付其他生物的药剂。

entries.definition: any chemical used to kill pests on crops
entries.definitionCN: 泛指对付作物害虫的化学药剂，是与 herbicide 同用 -cide 词尾的兄弟词

entries.definition: a chemical that kills insects
entries.definitionCN: 杀虫剂，专杀昆虫，与 herbicide 结构相同

entries.definition: a plant used for flavour or medicine
entries.definitionCN: 草本植物；草药，是 herbicide 的前半部分来源

entries.definition: a chemical that kills fungi
entries.definitionCN: 杀菌剂，同样由仿冒词干加 -cide 构成

entries.definition: the everyday name for a weed-killing product sold to gardeners
entries.definitionCN: 除草剂的家常用法，多指园艺店卖的除草用品，比 herbicide 更口语

entries.definition: a chemical that strips the leaves off plants
entries.definitionCN: 落叶剂，使植物叶片脱落，多用于军事，与除草剂目的不同

entries.definition: a substance added to help plants grow
entries.definitionCN: 肥料，帮助植物生长，与杀死植物的除草剂方向相反

normalIntro.en: Herbicide divides cleanly into herb plus -cide, and -cide is the killing ending shared with pesticide and insecticide.
normalIntro.cn: herbicide 可以干净地拆成 herb 加 -cide，而 -cide 就是与 pesticide、insecticide 共有的「杀死」词尾。

normal.en: The -cide ending means killing, so herbicide is the plant killer.
normal.cn: -cide 词尾表示「杀死」，所以 herbicide 就是「杀死植物」的东西。

normal.en: Compare insecticide for insects and fungicide for fungi: the first part names the victim.
normal.cn: 对比 insecticide 杀昆虫、fungicide 杀真菌：词的前半部分就是被消灭的对象。

normal.en: The plural is herbicides and the adjective is herbicidal.
normal.cn: 复数是 herbicides，形容词是 herbicidal。

normal.en: Herbicide resistance is the standard phrase for weeds that survive the spray.
normal.cn: herbicide resistance 是杂草在喷药后存活下来的标准说法。

normal.en: Spray herbicide and apply herbicide are the usual verb pairings.
normal.cn: 常见动宾搭配是 spray herbicide 与 apply herbicide。

abstract.en: Picture a mist drifting over a wheat field, with only the weeds curling brown.
abstract.cn: 想象雾气飘过麦田，只有杂草变成焦黄卷起。

abstract.en: Think of the word as a bottle label: herb on the left, the knife stroke on the right.
abstract.cn: 把这个词想成一张药瓶标签：左边写植物，右边画一刀砍下的记号。

abstract.en: Imagine rows of bottles on a shed shelf, one for every kind of enemy in the field.
abstract.cn: 想象棚屋架子上排着一列瓶子，田间每一种敌人都有对应的瓶子。

examples.en: Many farmers now reduce herbicide use and trust machinery instead.
examples.cn: 许多农场主如今减少除草剂的使用，转而依靠机械。

examples.en: The test measured herbicide residue in the soil.
examples.cn: 这项检测测量了土壤中的除草剂残留。

examples.en: Gardeners should read the label before applying any herbicide.
examples.cn: 园丁在使用任何除草剂之前都应阅读标签。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喝毙杀」——喝了就毙命、把草杀掉的东西，就是除草剂；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: herbicide 由拉丁语 herba（草木）与词尾 -cide（来自拉丁语 caedere，砍倒、杀死）构成，字面意为「能砍倒草木」，是十九世纪英语科技造词；英语中 herb 本身亦经古法语 herbe 上溯到 herba。

sensesIntro.en: Herbicide starts from the concrete bottle of weed killer, widens into the class name for crop chemicals, then to a land-management method, and finally to a contested public issue.
sensesIntro.cn: herbicide 从一瓶具体的除草剂出发，扩展为作物化学药剂的一个类别，再变成一种土地管理方法，最后成为一个有争议的公共议题。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fine mist settling on weeds while the crops beside them stay green.
core.cn: 核心意象：细雾落在杂草上，旁边的庄稼却照样青绿。

branches.en: The single bottle of weed killer is the basic sense.
branches.cn: 单瓶除草剂是最基本的义项。

branches.en: Grouping many such products makes the class sense.
branches.cn: 把许多这类产品归为一组，就得到类别义项。

branches.en: Using it as a method on railways or in forests gives the management sense.
branches.cn: 在铁路或森林中当作方法来用，就得到管理义项。

branches.en: Because the spray can drift, the word also names a public worry.
branches.cn: 因为药剂会飘散，这个词也就成了一项公共担忧的名称。

branches.en: One bottle and the whole shelf of crop chemicals share the same core image.
branches.cn: 一瓶药剂与整架子的作物化学品共享同一个核心意象。

intro.en: Herbicide is a compound of a Latin noun and a Latin verb-influenced ending, and it patterns with pesticide, insecticide, and fungicide.
intro.cn: herbicide 由一个拉丁语名词与一个源自拉丁语动词的词尾复合而成，与 pesticide、insecticide、fungicide 采用同一构词模式。

latinIntro.en: Latin herba supplies the plant half, and Latin caedere supplies the killing half behind the ending -cide.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 herba 提供「植物」的一半，拉丁语 caedere 提供词尾 -cide 背后「杀死」的一半。

items.example: Herba gives the first half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: herba 提供这个复合词的前半部分。

items.meaning: a plant used for flavour or medicine
items.example: Herb is the English form of Latin herba.
items.exampleCN: herb 是拉丁语 herba 的英语形式。

items.meaning: to cut, to strike down, to kill
items.example: Caedere lies behind the ending -cide.
items.exampleCN: caedere 藏在词尾 -cide 的背后。

items.meaning: a killing of, a killer of
items.meaningCN: 杀死……的行为；杀死……的东西
items.example: The suffix -cide turns stems into killing words.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -cide 把词干变成表示「杀死」的词。

items.example: Herbicide joins the plant to the killing ending.
items.exampleCN: herbicide 把植物与「杀死」词尾接在一起。

items.example: The suffix -al forms herbicidal.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 构成 herbicidal。

items.example: Herbicidal drops the final e before -al.
items.exampleCN: herbicidal 在加 -al 前省去了词尾的 e。

items.example: Pesticide is the wider class to which herbicide belongs.
items.exampleCN: pesticide 是 herbicide 所属的更大类别。

items.example: Fungicide copies the same plant-plus-cide pattern.
items.exampleCN: fungicide 沿用了同样的「对象加杀人词尾」模式。

definition_zh: 女主人公；女英雄；女杰；偶像
definition_en: a female hero, especially the main female character in a story, or a woman admired for brave or noble deeds
core_image: 舞台上聚光灯亮起，一位女性站在中央，台下所有人都望向她
scene: 小说读到最后一章，读者跟着那位女性走过饥饿、追捕与长途跋涉，终于在她救下整支队伍时合上书。The heroine of the novel survives every test and saves the whole crew.
sceneCN: 这里 heroine 是「女主人公」（第 1 个义项：文学作品里处于中心地位的女性人物）；句意：这部小说的女主人公经受住每一次考验，还救下了整支船队。

derivatives.zh: 由 hero 加 -ic 构成，义为「英勇的；英雄的」，与 heroine 同族
由 hero 加 -ism 构成，义为「英雄气概；英勇」
heroine 的阳性对应词，义为「男主人公；英雄」
heroine 与 worship 组合而成的复合名词，义为「对女英雄的崇拜」

senses.title: The main female character
senses.definition: the central female character in a novel, play, or film whose actions the story follows
senses.definitionCN: 小说、戏剧或电影中处于中心地位、情节围绕其行动展开的女性人物
senses.example: The heroine of the novel survives every test and saves the whole crew.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说的女主人公经受住每一次考验，还救下了整支船队。
senses.why: In Greek epic the hero is the figure at the centre of the story, and heroine simply gives that central figure a female form.
senses.whyCN: 在希腊史诗里，hero 是故事中心的人物，heroine 只是把这个中心人物换成女性来称呼。

senses.title: A supremely brave woman
senses.definition: a woman admired for courage, outstanding achievement, or noble self-sacrifice, especially in real life
senses.definitionCN: 因勇气、非凡成就或高尚的自我牺牲而受敬仰的女性，尤指现实生活中的
senses.example: She was honoured as a national heroine after the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水过后，她被尊为民族女英雄。
senses.why: The story sense drifts back into real life: a woman who does what the fiction heroine does earns the same label.
senses.whyCN: 故事义又回流到现实中：一位做出与小说女主角同样举动的女性，也得到同一个名号。

senses.title: The female lead of a work
senses.definition: the female performer who plays the leading part in a stage play, opera, or film
senses.definitionCN: 在舞台剧、歌剧或电影中担任主角的女性演员
senses.example: The young actress was cast as the heroine of the opera.
senses.exampleCN: 这位年轻女演员被选为这部歌剧的女主角。
senses.why: Once a role exists, people borrow the character name for the person who performs it.
senses.whyCN: 角色一旦固定下来，人们就借用角色名来称呼扮演它的演员。

senses.title: A woman someone admires
senses.definition: a woman regarded with devotion or surrounded by admiring attention, often playfully
senses.definitionCN: 被人倾心崇拜、备受瞩目的女性，常带一点玩笑意味
senses.example: To her younger cousins she was the heroine of the whole holiday.
senses.exampleCN: 对几个年幼的表妹来说，她就是整个假期的女主角。
senses.why: Admiration is the emotional core of the heroic sense, and it easily shrinks to a small everyday circle.
senses.whyCN: 敬佩之情是英雄义的情感核心，它很容易缩到日常的小圈子里。

intro.en: Heroine is the female form of hero, taken from Greek heros, a demi-god or noble warrior, with the feminine ending of Latin origin attached.
intro.cn: heroine 是 hero 的女性形式，源于希腊语 heros（半神或高贵武士），再缀上源自拉丁语的女性词尾。

items.en: heros first names a warrior of noble birth, and later a demi-god honoured with cult.
items.cn: heros 最初指出身高贵的武士，后来指受到祭祀的半神。

items.en: Latin hero becomes the form through which the word enters western Europe.
items.cn: 拉丁语 hero 成为这个词进入西欧语言的形态。

items.en: English hero names a great warrior or a man at the centre of a story.
items.cn: 英语 hero 指伟大的武士，或故事中心的人物。

items.en: The feminine ending -ine, as in heroine, marks a male word turned female.
items.cn: 女性词尾 -ine 使原本指男性的词变为指女性，heroine 就由此而来。

items.en: Heroine appears in English as the female counterpart of hero in plays and novels.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语中 heroine 作为 hero 的女性对应词出现，用于戏剧与小说。

items.en: The word spreads from fiction to real-life honours and to the stage.
items.cn: 现代英语中这个词从小说扩展到现实荣誉与舞台演出。

note.en: The first group gathers the hero family and a look-alike spelling; the second gathers the female roles she is compared with.
note.cn: 第一组收 hero 词族以及一个拼写相近的词；第二组收常用来比较的女性角色词。

entries.definition: a powerful illegal drug; it has no final e and is a different word
entries.definitionCN: 毒品海洛因；只差一个词尾 e，但只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a male hero or the central character of a story
entries.definitionCN: 男主人公；英雄；英雄人物，是 heroine 的阳性对应词

entries.definition: showing the courage of a hero
entries.definitionCN: 英勇的；英雄的，由同一词干加 -ic 构成

entries.definition: great courage or noble self-sacrifice
entries.definitionCN: 英雄气概；英勇行为

entries.definition: the leading character of a drama or story
entries.definitionCN: 主要人物；主角，中性词，不分男女，比 heroine 更学术

entries.definition: a person greatly admired, often from a distance
entries.definitionCN: 偶像；受崇敬的人，强调被仰慕，而不强调勇敢

entries.definition: a person whose behaviour others try to copy
entries.definitionCN: 榜样；行为示范者，强调可效仿，而不是英雄事迹

normalIntro.en: Heroine is hero plus the feminine ending -ine, so it is the hero of a story or a cause viewed as a woman.
normalIntro.cn: heroine 是 hero 加上女性词尾 -ine，也就是以女性身份出现的英雄。

normal.en: Strip the -ine from heroine and the hero family appears: hero, heroic, heroism.
normal.cn: 剥掉词尾 -ine 就能看到整个词族：hero、heroic、heroism。

normal.en: The feminine -ine also appears in words renamed from the male form, like heroine from hero.
normal.cn: 这个女性词尾 -ine 也出现在由男性形态改写而来的词里，例如由 hero 变成 heroine。

normal.en: One extra e separates the actress from the drug: heroine and heroin.
normal.cn: 多一个词尾 e 就把女主人公和毒品分开了：heroine 与 heroin。

normal.en: The plural is heroines, with no apostrophe.
normal.cn: 复数是 heroines，不加任何符号。

normal.en: A national heroine is praised in public, while the heroine of a novel stays on the page.
normal.cn: national heroine 是在现实中受表彰的人，小说的 heroine 则只活在书页里。

abstract.en: Picture the curtain lifting with one woman alone under the light.
abstract.cn: 想象幕布升起，灯光下只有一个女人站在那里。

abstract.en: Imagine a village crowd cheering someone who stepped forward when no one else would.
abstract.cn: 想象全村人围着一位在没人敢上前时挺身而出的人欢呼。

abstract.en: Think of a playbill where one name is printed larger than the rest.
abstract.cn: 想象一张节目单，其中一个名字印得比别的大。

examples.en: The heroine of the story refuses to give up her farm.
examples.cn: 故事的女主人公拒绝放弃自己的农场。

examples.en: She is remembered as a heroine who carried children out of the fire.
examples.cn: 她被人们铭记为把孩子们从火里救出来的女英雄。

examples.en: Critics argued that the play needed a stronger heroine.
examples.cn: 评论家认为这出戏需要一个更有力量的女主人公。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「黑肉因」——台上一身黑衣的女主角，因为她才有人来看戏；这只取音近，与词源无关。

root: heroine 由希腊语 heros（半神、高贵武士）经拉丁语 hero 进入英语，再加拉丁系统的女性词尾 -ine 构成，与 hero、heroic、heroism 同源；阳性形式为 hero。

sensesIntro.en: Heroine begins as the leading woman of a story, widens to women admired for bravery in real life, then turns into the stage role and the admired person.
sensesIntro.cn: heroine 先从故事里的女主角出发，扩展到现实中因勇敢而受敬仰的女性，再变成舞台角色与被崇拜的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a woman alone at the centre of the stage under a single light.
core.cn: 核心意象：一位女性独自站在舞台中央的灯光下。

branches.en: The leading woman of a story is the literary sense.
branches.cn: 故事里的女主角是文学义项。

branches.en: Courage in real life makes the real-world heroine.
branches.cn: 现实生活中的勇气造就现实中的女英雄。

branches.en: The role itself lends its name to the performer.
branches.cn: 角色名被借来称呼扮演者。

branches.en: Admiration shrinks the grand title to a small and warm one.
branches.cn: 敬慕之心把宏大的称号缩小成亲切的小称呼。

branches.en: The woman in the book and the woman in the crowd share one core image.
branches.cn: 书里的女性与人群中的女性共享同一个核心意象。

intro.en: Heroine is hero plus the feminine ending -ine, and its family runs through hero, heroic, heroism, and a famous spelling trap.
intro.cn: heroine 是 hero 加女性词尾 -ine 构成的，它的词族包括 hero、heroic、heroism，还有一个著名的拼写陷阱。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Greek, but the feminine ending arrived through Latin adjectives, so heroine sits between Greek and Latin forms.
latinIntro.cn: 词干来自希腊语，但女性词尾经拉丁语形容词传入，所以 heroine 处在希腊语与拉丁语形态之间。

items.example: Heros is the Greek head of the family.
items.exampleCN: heros 是这一词族的希腊语源头。

items.example: Latin hero carries the Greek word westward.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 hero 把希腊词带向西方。

items.example: Hero enters English in the late medieval period.
items.exampleCN: hero 在中世纪末期进入英语。

items.meaning: forming the feminine of a noun
items.example: The ending -ine turns a masculine word feminine.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ine 把阳性词变成女性形式。

items.example: Heroine keeps the e of the stem before -ine.
items.exampleCN: heroine 在加 -ine 前保留了词干的 e。

items.meaningCN: 具有……性质的形容词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ic forms heroic.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ic 构成 heroic。

items.example: Heroic describes brave action rather than a person.
items.exampleCN: heroic 描述英勇的行为，而不是某个人。

items.meaningCN: 表示性质或行为方式的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ism forms heroism.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ism 构成 heroism。

items.example: Heroism is the quality behind the hero.
items.exampleCN: heroism 是英雄背后的品质。

definition_zh: 犹豫；迟疑；停顿；踌躇
definition_en: the act of pausing before doing something, often because of doubt, uncertainty, or unwillingness
core_image: 一只手停在半空，伸向门口又把回去，指尖在原地轻轻晃动
scene: 门外有人问她要不要现在就进来，她握住把手，却迟迟没有转动。After a moment of hesitation, she opened the door and stepped inside.
sceneCN: 这里 hesitation 是「犹豫」（第 1 个义项：因拿不定主意而在行动前停住）；句意：犹豫片刻之后，她推开门走了进去。

collocations.phrase: have no hesitation in doing something

derivatives.zh: hesitation 的动词形式，义为「犹豫；迟疑」
hesitate 加 -ant 构成，义为「迟疑的；犹豫不决的」
hesitant 加 -ly 构成，义为「迟疑地；犹豫地」
hesitant 加 -cy 构成，义为「犹豫；迟疑不决」，比 hesitation 更书面

senses.title: Pausing in doubt
senses.definition: a pause before acting or deciding, caused by uncertainty or divided feelings
senses.definitionCN: 因为拿不准或心里有分歧，在行动或做决定之前停住
senses.example: After a moment of hesitation, she opened the door and stepped inside.
senses.exampleCN: 犹豫片刻之后，她推开门走了进去。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to stick fast, so hesitation is the mind caught as if glued to one spot before it can move.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词意为「黏住、卡住不动」，所以犹豫就是心思像被粘在原地，动不起来。

senses.title: A sign of doubt in manner
senses.definition: a slight pause, stammer, or awkwardness in speech or movement that shows doubt
senses.definitionCN: 言语或动作中的短暂停顿、结巴或不自然，透露出心里没底
senses.example: He answered with a hesitation that made everyone look up.
senses.exampleCN: 他回答时迟疑了一下，所有人都抬起了头。
senses.why: From the act of pausing, the word shifts to the little stumble that betrays the pause, much as a sigh betrays relief.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从「停住」的动作，转到暴露这次停顿的小磕绊，就像一声叹气泄露了宽慰。

senses.title: An unwilling but accepted delay
senses.definition: a short delay in doing something, sometimes more a matter of courtesy or caution than of doubt
senses.definitionCN: 做事时出现的短促延迟，有时更多出于礼貌或谨慎，而非真的拿不定主意
senses.example: He agreed to join the team without hesitation.
senses.exampleCN: 他毫不犹豫地同意加入这个团队。
senses.why: Because a pause can be wise as well as weak, the word also covers the careful delay people allow themselves on purpose.
senses.whyCN: 因为停顿既可能是软弱，也可能是明智，这个词也涵盖人们有意的谨慎等待。

intro.en: Hesitation comes from Latin haesitatio, a sticking fast, built on the verb haesitare, a frequentative of haerere, to stick.
intro.cn: hesitation 来自拉丁语 haesitatio（黏着、卡住），由动词 haesitare 构成，而 haesitare 是 haerere（黏附）的反复体形式。

items.en: haerere means to stick or cling, and gives English adhere and inherent.
items.cn: haerere 意为黏附、贴住，也衍生出英语的 adhere 与 inherent。

items.en: haesitare is the frequentative form, to keep sticking, hence to be at a loss or stammer.
items.cn: haesitare 是反复体，表示反复黏住，也就引申为拿不定主意、说话卡住。

items.en: The abstract noun adds the ending -tio to name the state of being stuck.
items.cn: 抽象名词 haesitatio 加后缀 -tio，用来指「卡住的状态」。

items.en: English hesitation names the act of pausing before acting.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语中 hesitation 指行动之前的停顿。

items.en: Modern usage adds the idiomatic phrase without hesitation.
items.cn: 现代用法加上了「毫不犹豫」这类固定说法。

note.en: The first group gathers the hesitate family; the second gathers words about delay, doubt, and their opposites.
note.cn: 第一组收 hesitate 的动词与形容词词族；第二组收表示耽搁、疑虑及其反义的词。

entries.definition: to pause before acting because of doubt
entries.definitionCN: 因拿不准而在行动前停下，是 hesitation 的动词

entries.definition: unsure and slow to act or speak
entries.definitionCN: 迟疑的；犹豫不决的

entries.definition: in a way that shows doubt or unwillingness
entries.definitionCN: 迟疑地；犹豫地

entries.definition: the quality of being slow or unwilling to act
entries.definitionCN: 犹豫不决的状态，比 hesitation 更书面

entries.definition: the time for which something is put off
entries.definitionCN: 耽搁；延迟，强调时间被拖长，不一定有疑虑

entries.definition: an uncertain feeling about whether something is true
entries.definitionCN: 怀疑；疑虑，是犹豫常有的内在原因

entries.definition: a firm decision to do something
entries.definitionCN: 决心；果断，是犹豫的反面

normalIntro.en: Hesitation is the noun behind hesitate, and both go back to a Latin verb that means to stick.
normalIntro.cn: hesitation 是 hesitate 的名词形式，两者都源自一个意为「黏住」的拉丁语动词。

normal.en: The -tion ending turns the verb hesitate into the noun hesitation.
normal.cn: 词尾 -tion 把动词 hesitate 变成名词 hesitation。

normal.en: Without hesitation means at once, with no pausing, and is the most common phrase.
normal.cn: without hesitation 意为立刻、不停顿，是最常见的搭配。

normal.en: The adjective is hesitant and the adverb is hesitantly.
normal.cn: 形容词是 hesitant，副词是 hesitantly。

normal.en: Keep the s and the t: hesitate, not hezitate, even though the sound is the same.
normal.cn: 拼写保留 s 和 t：是 hesitate，虽然读音听起来一样也不写成别的字母。

normal.en: The noun counts as a pause, so one uses a moment of hesitation.
normal.cn: 这个词指一次停顿，所以常说 a moment of hesitation。

abstract.en: Picture a shoe lifted to take a step and hanging there, unsure.
abstract.cn: 想象一只鞋抬起来要迈步，却停在半空拿不定主意。

abstract.en: Think of a hand on a door handle that turns it halfway and stops.
abstract.cn: 想一只握住门把手的手，转到一半就停住了。

abstract.en: Imagine a sentence begun, then a long empty pause before the next word.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话开了头，接着是很长的一段空白，才说出下一个词。

examples.en: There was a brief hesitation before she gave her answer.
examples.cn: 她在给出答案之前有短暂的犹豫。

examples.en: The company announced the change without hesitation.
examples.cn: 公司毫不犹豫地宣布了这项变动。

examples.en: Her hesitation was visible in every sentence she spoke.
examples.cn: 她说的每一句话都透露出犹豫。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「黑子推婶」——黑子想把婶婶推出去，手伸到一半又缩回来，正是犹豫；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: hesitation 由拉丁语 haerere（黏附、贴住）的反复体 haesitare（反复黏住、卡住、说话打结）加名词词尾 -tio 构成，核心义「被黏住动不了」，故为犹豫；同源词还有 adhere、inherent。

sensesIntro.en: Hesitation begins with the concrete pause before a decision, moves to the small stumble that shows doubt, and ends with the deliberate delay that caution or courtesy allows.
sensesIntro.cn: hesitation 从做决定前那一次具体的停顿出发，转到暴露疑虑的小磕绊，最后落到谨慎或礼貌造成的刻意延迟。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand that reaches for the door and stops in mid-air.
core.cn: 核心意象：伸向门的手停在半空。

branches.en: A pause in doubt is the central sense.
branches.cn: 拿不准而停住是中心义项。

branches.en: The pause leaking into speech or movement gives the manner sense.
branches.cn: 停顿渗进言语和动作，就有了神态义项。

branches.en: A pause kept on purpose becomes a cautious delay.
branches.cn: 有意保留的停顿，就成为一种谨慎的耽搁。

branches.en: The pause in the mind and the stumble in the voice are two faces of one moment.
branches.cn: 心里的停顿与嘴上的磕绊，是同一瞬间的两面。

branches.en: Both hesitation and precaution keep the moment still, one from doubt and one from care.
branches.cn: 犹豫与谨慎都会让那一刻停住，一个出于疑虑，一个出于小心。

intro.en: Hesitation is the abstract noun built on hesitate, and the family runs through the adjective hesitant and the adverb hesitantly.
intro.cn: hesitation 是由 hesitate 构成的抽象名词，词族包括形容词 hesitant 与副词 hesitantly。

latinIntro.en: Latin haerere gives the sticking core; the frequentative haesitare repeats that sticking, and haesitatio names the state.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 haerere 提供「黏住」的核心，反复体 haesitare 表示反复黏着，haesitatio 则指这种状态。

items.example: Haerere is the base root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: haerere 是整族词的根。

items.meaning: to keep sticking, to be at a loss
items.example: The frequentative repeats the sticking until it becomes doubt.
items.exampleCN: 反复体把「黏着」重复到变成疑虑。

items.meaningCN: 构成表示动作的抽象名词
items.example: The suffix -tio turns the verb into a noun of action.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -tio 把动词变成表动作的名词。

items.meaning: the act of pausing in doubt
items.example: Hesitation is the noun of the pausing state.
items.exampleCN: hesitation 是「停住」这一状态的名词。

items.example: Hesitate is the verb back-formed and kept in English.
items.exampleCN: hesitate 是保留在英语里的动词形式。

items.meaningCN: 处于某种状态的形容词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ant forms hesitant.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ant 构成 hesitant。

items.meaning: slow to act because of doubt
items.example: Hesitant describes the person, not the pause.
items.exampleCN: hesitant 描述人，而不是那次停顿。

items.meaningCN: 以……的方式构成的副词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ly forms hesitantly.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 hesitantly。

items.meaning: in a doubtful or unwilling way
items.example: Hesitantly describes how an action is done.
items.exampleCN: hesitantly 描述动作是怎样做的。

latinEntries.meaning: to be at a loss, to stammer

definition_zh: 启发式的；试探性的；启发法；经验法则
definition_en: allowing a person to discover or learn something for themselves, or using a practical rule of thumb rather than a strictly proven method
core_image: 一只手在空中摸索着往前走，边走边找到路
scene: 做题时学生没有套公式，而是先猜个大概再检验，老师说这是一种启发式的思路。Facing the puzzle, the students guessed first and then tested, and the teacher praised this heuristic way of thinking.
sceneCN: 这里 heuristic 是「启发式的、靠经验摸索的」（第 1 个义项：帮助人自己发现问题、找到方法的）；句意：面对那道题，学生们先猜后验，老师称赞了这种启发式的思路。

pos.zh: 启发式的；试探性的；凭经验摸索的

derivatives.zh: 启发法；经验法则（常用复数，指一整套凭经验摸索的办法）
以启发式的方式；凭经验摸索地
启发主义；以求知推动思考的主张（较生僻）

senses.title: Helping learners discover for themselves
senses.definition: describing a method of teaching that encourages students to work things out for themselves instead of being told the answer
senses.definitionCN: 形容一种教学方式，鼓励学生自己摸索出答案，而不是直接被告知
senses.example: The teacher used a heuristic method so that pupils could find the rule by themselves.
senses.exampleCN: 老师采用启发式教学法，让学生自己找出规律。
senses.why: The Greek root heuriskein means to find, so a heuristic method leads the learner to the discovery rather than handing over the result.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语词根 heuriskein 意为「找到」，所以启发式方法是把学习者引向答案，而不是把结论直接塞过去。

senses.title: A rule of thumb that works well enough
senses.definition: a practical shortcut or rule that gives a good enough answer quickly, without fully checking every possibility
senses.definitionCN: 一种实用的捷径或法则，能快速给出足够好的答案，而不必逐一验证所有可能
senses.example: As a heuristic, the team always tests the cheapest option first.
senses.exampleCN: 作为一条经验法则，团队总是先测试成本最低的方案。
senses.why: In problem solving the word names a rule that helps you find a workable answer fast, like a thumb on the page rather than a full search.
senses.whyCN: 在解题语境里，这个词指能快速帮你「找到」可用答案的法则，像用拇指按住书页快速翻找，而不是穷尽搜索。

senses.title: Trial and error in computing
senses.definition: a technique in computer science that finds an acceptable solution by intelligent guessing when a perfect method is too slow
senses.definitionCN: 计算机科学中的一种技术：当精确方法太慢时，用智能猜测找到可接受的解
senses.example: The heuristic algorithm finds a good route in seconds, though not always the shortest one.
senses.exampleCN: 这种启发式算法几秒内就能找到一条不错的路线，虽然不一定最短。
senses.why: Because the word stresses finding rather than proving, engineers use it for shortcuts that get close enough quickly.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个词强调「找到」而非「证明」，工程师用它来命名那些能快速逼近答案的捷径。

intro.en: Heuristic goes back to the Greek heuriskein, to find, and was named by Albert Neisser in 1880 for a method of discovery.
intro.cn: heuristic 源于希腊语 heuriskein（找到），一般认为最早由德国医生阿尔贝特·奈瑟尔在 1880 年用来命名一种发现式的解题方法。

items.en: Heuriskein means to find or discover.
items.cn: heuriskein 意为找到、发现。

items.en: Eureka, the famous discovery shout, comes from the same verb.
items.cn: 著名的惊喜呼声「尤里卡」正是出自同一个动词。

items.en: Scholars build the Latin adjective heuristicus on the Greek root.
items.cn: 学者们在希腊词根上造出拉丁语形容词 heuristicus。

items.en: The term is used to describe a method of finding solutions.
items.cn: 该词被用来命名一种寻找解法的办法。

items.en: English adopts it first for education, then for computing algorithms.
items.cn: 英语先把它用于教育学，后来又用于计算机算法。

note.en: Heuristic keeps the idea of finding; the look-alikes are the eureka word and related Greek forms, while near meanings are about practical rules and trial.
note.cn: heuristic 保留了「找到」的意象；形近词是与「尤里卡」一词相关的希腊形式，近义词则是讲实用规则与试探的说法。

entries.definition: an exclamation used when one has found or discovered something
entries.definitionCN: 找到了、实验成功时的惊叹语

entries.definition: the study or practice of methods for finding solutions
entries.definitionCN: 启发法；寻找解法的研究

entries.definition: famous or important in history
entries.definitionCN: 有历史意义的（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: a rough practical rule based on experience
entries.definitionCN: 经验法则；粗略的实用办法

entries.definition: a principle that controls how something is done
entries.definitionCN: 规则；准则

entries.definition: based on observation and experiment rather than pure theory
entries.definitionCN: 以经验为依据的；实证的

normalIntro.en: Heuristic carries the Greek act of finding, so it marks any method that leads you to a discovery.
normalIntro.cn: heuristic 携带着希腊语「找到」的动作，所以它标记一切把你引向发现的方法。

normal.en: Remember eureka: both heuristic and eureka point back to the Greek verb meaning to find.
normal.cn: 记住「尤里卡」：heuristic 与它同源于希腊语中意为「找到」的动词。

normal.en: A heuristic approach is a teaching or working style, so it pairs with approach, method, and device.
normal.cn: heuristic approach 指教学或工作风格，因此常与 approach、method、device 搭配。

normal.en: As a noun, heuristics often appears in the plural: computer programs rely on heuristics.
normal.cn: 作名词时常用复数 heuristics：computer programs rely on heuristics 意为程序依靠启发式方法。

normal.en: Compare heuristic with empirical: both trust experience, but heuristic names the shortcut, empirical names the evidence.
normal.cn: 对比 empirical：两者都信任经验，但 heuristic 指捷径本身，empirical 指证据来源。

normal.en: The adverb heuristically describes solving a problem by guided trial.
normal.cn: 副词 heuristically 描述用有引导的试探来解决问题。

abstract.en: Picture a torch lighting the next few steps of an unknown path.
abstract.cn: 想象一支火把只照亮未知小路的前几步。

abstract.en: Imagine a sailor judging depth by a knotted rope in his hand.
abstract.cn: 想象水手用手中打着结的绳索判断水深。

abstract.en: See a map that shows a dotted shortcut beside the long exact road.
abstract.cn: 想象一幅地图，在漫长的精确路线旁画出一条虚线捷径。

examples.en: Good teachers prefer a heuristic approach to lecturing.
examples.cn: 好老师更倾向于启发式教学而非单纯讲授。

examples.en: Experienced doctors use a heuristic to decide which tests to order first.
examples.cn: 经验丰富的医生会用一条经验法则来决定先做哪些检查。

examples.en: The heuristics saved the team hours of computation.
examples.cn: 这些启发式方法为团队省下了数小时的计算。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「黑又立」——老师启发你「黑」灯摸索、自己「立」起来找答案；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 heuriskein（找到、发现）→ 拉丁语 heuristicus → 19 世纪借用入英语；同族有「尤里卡」。核心义「引领去找到」。

sensesIntro.en: Heuristic starts as a teaching style that leads to discovery, then becomes a practical rule of thumb, and finally a computing shortcut.
sensesIntro.cn: heuristic 先是一种引向发现的教学方式，再演变为实用的经验法则，最后成为计算机里的近似算法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand feeling its way forward and finding the path as it goes.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手摸索着向前，边走边找到路。

branches.en: Teaching that lets students find the answer is the educational sense.
branches.cn: 让学生自己找到答案的教学方式是教育义项。

branches.en: A rule of thumb is the everyday problem solving sense.
branches.cn: 经验法则是日常解题中的义项。

branches.en: A fast approximate search is the technical sense.
branches.cn: 快速的近似搜索是技术义项。

branches.en: Both a teacher and a rule of thumb guide someone towards a workable answer.
branches.cn: 老师与经验法则都把人引向一个可用的答案。

branches.en: Both practical rules and algorithms trade perfection for speed.
branches.cn: 实用法则与算法都以牺牲完美来换取速度。

intro.en: Heuristic is built on the Greek verb for finding, with English relatives in heuristics and heuristically.
intro.cn: heuristic 建立在希腊语「找到」动词之上，英语同族有 heuristics 与 heuristically。

latinIntro.en: Latin never had the Greek word; the adjective heuristicus was formed by modern scholars on the Greek root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语原本没有这个希腊词，形容词 heuristicus 是近代学者依据希腊词根新造的形式。

items.example: Heuriskein gives the finding image.
items.exampleCN: heuriskein 提供「找到」的意象。

items.example: Heuresis names the act of finding.
items.exampleCN: heuresis 指发现这一动作。

items.meaning: relating to, in the manner of
items.example: The suffix -istic turns the root into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -istic 把词根变成形容词。

items.example: Heuristic describes a guiding method.
items.exampleCN: heuristic 描述一种引导性方法。

items.example: Heuristics means a set of such rules.
items.exampleCN: heuristics 指一整套这类法则。

items.example: Heuristically keeps the adjective sense as an adverb.
items.exampleCN: heuristically 以副词形式保留形容词语义。

items.example: Eureka shares the finding root.
items.exampleCN: eureka 共享「找到」词根。

items.example: Heuristic search is a computing technique.
items.exampleCN: 启发式搜索是一种计算技术。

definition_zh: 打嗝；呃逆；小问题；小故障
definition_en: a sudden sharp intake of breath that makes a hic sound, or a small temporary problem
core_image: 一口气猛地把横膈膜抽紧，喉咙里发出一声「呃」
scene: 会议刚开始，网络就掉了一下，大家笑着说这只是个小插曲。The meeting had barely started when the video link dropped, and everyone called it just a hiccup.
sceneCN: 这里 hiccup 是「小问题、小故障」（第 3 个义项：暂时性的小毛病）；句意：会议刚开始视频连线就断了，大家都说这不过是个小插曲。

pos.zh: 打嗝；呃逆；小问题；小故障

derivatives.zh: 打嗝似的；一顿一顿的；不顺畅的
打嗝（旧式拼写，读音与 hiccup 相同）

senses.title: The sudden breath with a hic sound
senses.definition: a sudden sharp movement of the diaphragm that pulls in air and makes a short hic sound in the throat
senses.definitionCN: 横膈膜突然收缩吸入空气，在喉咙里发出短促「呃」声的生理现象
senses.example: He got the hiccups after drinking too fast.
senses.exampleCN: 他喝得太快，打起了嗝。
senses.why: The word is an imitation of the sound itself, so the basic sense is simply that jerky body noise.
senses.whyCN: 这个词直接模仿声音本身，所以最基本的义项就是那一声身体发出的抽动噪音。

senses.title: The verb of hiccuping
senses.definition: to make the sudden hic sound, usually again and again for a short time
senses.definitionCN: 发出这种短促的「呃」声，通常在一小段时间内反复出现
senses.example: The baby hiccuped twice and then fell asleep.
senses.exampleCN: 婴儿打了两个嗝，然后睡着了。
senses.why: Any sound word can become a verb, so the action of producing the sound is the second sense.
senses.whyCN: 任何拟声词都可以转为动词，因此发出这种声音的动作就成了第二个义项。

senses.title: A small temporary problem
senses.definition: a small problem or interruption that soon passes, especially in a plan, process, or market
senses.definitionCN: 很快就过去的小问题或短暂中断，尤指计划、进程或市场中的小波折
senses.example: There was a hiccup in the payment system, but the order went through.
senses.exampleCN: 支付系统出了个小故障，但订单还是完成了。
senses.why: A hiccup interrupts the smooth rhythm of breathing for a moment, just as a small fault interrupts a smooth process, and it passes just as quickly.
senses.whyCN: 打嗝只是短暂打断呼吸的平稳节奏，正如小故障打断顺畅的流程，而且同样转瞬即逝，于是被引申为「小问题」。

intro.en: Hiccup is a sound imitating word; its earlier form hiccup was respelled in the sixteenth century from hiccough, which borrowed the spelling of cough.
intro.cn: hiccup 是拟声词；它十六世纪之前的写法 hiccup 又被改拼成 hiccough，只是借用了 cough 的拼写，读音不变。

items.en: The word imitates the short sound made in the throat.
items.cn: 这个词模仿喉咙里发出的短促声音。

items.en: Hiccup appears in English writing as a sound word.
items.cn: hiccup 在十六世纪的英语文献中以拟声词面貌出现。

items.en: The spelling hiccough is adopted by false analogy with cough, without changing the pronunciation.
items.cn: 受 cough 的拼写影响，出现了 hiccough 这种错误类比拼法，读音并未改变。

items.en: Hiccup becomes the usual standard spelling again.
items.cn: hiccup 重新成为通行的标准拼写。

items.en: The word extends from the body noise to small problems in plans and markets.
items.cn: 该词从身体发出的声音扩展到计划与市场中的小问题。

note.en: Hiccup has a sound-imitation family and a group of words for small problems; the near meanings are not about the body at all.
note.cn: hiccup 有拟声词家族，也有一组表示「小问题」的近义词；后者与身体无关。

entries.definition: an old spelling of hiccup with the same pronunciation
entries.definitionCN: hiccup 的旧式拼写，读音相同

entries.definition: repeated hiccups, or the plural form
entries.definitionCN: 接连不断的打嗝；复数形式

entries.definition: the act of collecting someone or something
entries.definitionCN: 接送；捡起（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: a small fault in a machine or system
entries.definitionCN: 机器或系统的小故障

entries.definition: a problem that delays progress
entries.definitionCN: 挫折；阻碍

entries.definition: an unexpected small difficulty
entries.definitionCN: 意外的障碍；小麻烦

normalIntro.en: Hiccup is the sound in the throat written down, and the sound can also stand for a brief slip in a plan.
normalIntro.cn: hiccup 就是把喉咙里的声音写下来，而这声音也能代表计划中一次短暂的磕绊。

normal.en: Hiccup and hic are one sound, so the whole word sounds like the thing it names.
normal.cn: hiccup 与 hic 是同一个声音，整个词读起来就像它所指的现象。

normal.en: Have the hiccups is the fixed phrase for the body sense; a hiccup in the process is the figurative one.
normal.cn: have the hiccups 是身体义项的固定搭配，a hiccup in the process 则是比喻用法。

normal.en: The verb doubles its final consonant in British spelling: hiccupped, but hiccuped in many American texts.
normal.cn: 动词过去式在英式拼写中双写末尾辅音写作 hiccupped，美式常见 hiccuped。

normal.en: The spelling hiccough borrows the look of cough but keeps the sound of cup.
normal.cn: 拼写 hiccough 借用了 cough 的外形，读音仍是 cup 那一套。

normal.en: A minor hiccup is a small problem that does not stop anything for long.
normal.cn: a minor hiccup 指不会长时间阻碍事情的小问题。

abstract.en: Picture a speaker pausing mid sentence to catch a breath.
abstract.cn: 想象说话人说到一半忽然一顿，去换口气。

abstract.en: Feel the chest jerking once while the sentence carries on.
abstract.cn: 感受胸口猛地抽动一下，而语句还在继续。

abstract.en: See a smooth train line with one short bump in the rails.
abstract.cn: 想象一条平坦的铁路线，轨道上只隆起一小块。

examples.en: She hiccups whenever she eats too quickly.
examples.cn: 她吃得太快时就会打嗝。

examples.en: The launch went ahead without a hiccup.
examples.cn: 发布顺利进行，毫无波折。

examples.en: A minor hiccup in the supply chain delayed one shipment.
examples.cn: 供应链上的一个小问题耽误了一批货。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「嘿卡扑」——打嗝时喉咙里就「嘿」地卡一下、扑腾一声；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拟声词，模仿喉咙里短促的吸气声；约十六世纪见于英语，后有一度写作 hiccough（借 cough 拼写）。核心义「一阵短促的抽动」。

sensesIntro.en: Hiccup first names the body noise, then the act of making it, and finally any small problem that interrupts a smooth process.
sensesIntro.cn: hiccup 先指身体发出的那种声音，再指发出这种声音的动作，最后指打断顺畅进程的任何小问题。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the chest jerking once with a short hic, then going on as before.
core.cn: 核心意象：胸口猛地一抽，发出一声「呃」，随后照常继续。

branches.en: The body noise is the literal sense.
branches.cn: 身体发出的声音是字面义项。

branches.en: The action of hiccuping is the verb sense.
branches.cn: 打嗝的动作是动词义项。

branches.en: A minor problem in a plan is the figurative sense.
branches.cn: 计划中的小问题是比喻义项。

branches.en: The sound and the act it names form one single physical event.
branches.cn: 那声音与发出声音的动作构成同一个生理事件。

branches.en: Both meanings describe a short interruption that soon passes.
branches.cn: 两个义项都描述很快过去的一次短暂打断。

intro.en: Hiccup is not built from classical affixes; it is a sound word, with the variant spelling hiccough made by false analogy with cough.
intro.cn: hiccup 并非由古典词缀构成，而是拟声词；变体拼写 hiccough 是受 cough 影响而产生的错误类比。

latinIntro.en: The word has no Latin ancestor; older medical Latin used singultus for hiccups, a word of uncertain origin.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语祖形；古医学拉丁语用 singultus 表示打嗝，该词来源不确定。

items.meaning: the short sound in the throat
items.example: Hic is the sound part of the word.
items.exampleCN: hic 是这个拟声词的音形部分。

items.meaning: a sudden breath with a hic sound
items.example: Hiccup names the bodily noise.
items.exampleCN: hiccup 指身体发出的那种声音。

items.example: Hiccups usually means a bout of them.
items.exampleCN: hiccups 通常指一阵连续的打嗝。

items.example: Hiccuped is the common American past form.
items.exampleCN: hiccuped 是常见的美式过去式。

items.example: Hiccupping doubles the final consonant in British spelling.
items.exampleCN: 英式拼写中 hiccupping 双写末尾辅音。

items.example: Hiccough borrows the letters of cough.
items.exampleCN: hiccough 借用了 cough 的字母。

items.example: The suffix -y forms the adjective hiccupy.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 构成形容词 hiccupy。

items.meaning: to force air out of the lungs noisily
items.example: Cough shaped the false spelling hiccough.
items.exampleCN: cough 影响了 hiccough 这一错误拼写。

definition_zh: 山核桃；山核桃木；山核桃木制的
definition_en: a tall North American tree with hard strong wood and nuts, or the wood itself
core_image: 一根又硬又韧的山核桃木斧柄，被举起来劈下
scene: 祖父把木柄斧头递给我，说这柄是山核桃木做的，握着特别稳。Grandpa handed me the axe and said its handle was made of hickory, which grips with surprising steady balance.
sceneCN: 这里 hickory 是「山核桃木」（第 2 个义项：这种树坚硬结实的木材）；句意：祖父把斧头递给我，说这斧柄是山核桃木做的，握起来格外稳当。

pos.zh: 山核桃；山核桃树；山核桃木

collocations.zh: 用山核桃木熏制的（风味）

derivatives.zh: 山核桃树的复数，指成片的山核桃林
山核桃的果实（复合名词）
碧根果（山核桃属的另一种坚果，与 hickory 同属不同种）

senses.title: The tree and its nuts
senses.definition: a tall tree of the walnut family native to eastern North America, known for its tough shelled nuts
senses.definitionCN: 北美东部土生的一种高大乔木，属胡桃科，以硬壳坚果著称
senses.example: Squirrels stash hickory nuts under the porch every autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 每年秋天松鼠都把山核桃藏在门廊下。
senses.why: The name first belongs to the tree and its nuts, from which every other sense grows.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字最初就属于这种树和它的果实，其他义项都由此生长出来。

senses.title: Hard wood for tools
senses.definition: the hard and heavy timber of the hickory tree, used for tool handles, sporting goods, and furniture
senses.definitionCN: 山核桃树坚硬沉重的木材，用于工具手柄、体育器材和家具
senses.example: A hickory handle lasts far longer than a pine one.
senses.exampleCN: 山核桃木手柄比松木手柄耐用得多。
senses.why: Once the tree is valued for its timber, the material itself takes the name, and its hardness makes the word stand for toughness.
senses.whyCN: 当这种树因木材而被看重，木材本身也承袭了这个名字，硬度则让这个词带上了「坚韧」的意味。

senses.title: Smoke from burning hickory
senses.definition: the strong sweet smoke produced by burning hickory wood, used to flavour meat
senses.definitionCN: 燃烧山核桃木产生的浓郁甜香烟雾，用来给肉类调味
senses.example: The ribs were slow cooked over hickory for the whole afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 排骨用山核桃木慢火熏了整整一下午。
senses.why: Barbecue cooks use hickory chips the way others use oak, so the wood name shifts into the flavour of the smoke.
senses.whyCN: 烧烤师把山核桃木屑当作橡木屑来用，于是木材名进一步转移为烟熏风味。

intro.en: Hickory comes from the Algonquian word for a certain nut or wood, recorded in Virginia English in 1618 and reshaped in English spelling over the next century.
intro.cn: hickory 来自阿尔冈昆诸语中表示某种坚果或木材的词，一般认为其英语记录最早见于 1618 年前后弗吉尼亚地区的文献，此后一个世纪里英语拼写几经变化。

items.en: An Algonquian word for a battered nut or its wood is borrowed by colonists.
items.cn: 殖民者借入了阿尔冈昆语中表示捣碎坚果或其木材的词。

items.en: Early records write forms such as pohickory for the nut and its food.
items.cn: 早期文献把它写作 pohickory 之类的形式，指这种坚果及以其制成的食物。

items.en: Similar spellings like hiccory appear for the tree and its wood.
items.cn: 十七世纪出现 hiccory 等拼写，用来指这种树及其木材。

items.en: The modern spelling hickory settles for the tree, the wood, and the nut.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，hickory 这一拼写固定下来，用于树、木材与坚果。

items.en: The wood becomes standard for axe handles and baseball bats, strengthening images of toughness.
items.cn: 这种木材成为斧柄与棒球棒的标准用料，进一步强化了「坚韧」的意象。

note.en: Hickory belongs to the nut and timber words, and its look-alikes are chiefly other tree and nut names rather than its relatives.
note.cn: hickory 属于坚果与木材一类词，它的形近词主要是其他树名与坚果名，而不是同源词。

entries.definition: the plural form of the tree name
entries.definitionCN: 山核桃树名的复数形式

entries.definition: an early colonial spelling of the nut name
entries.definitionCN: 早期殖民时期的旧拼写，指这种坚果

entries.definition: a small mark or gadget, mainly in informal use
entries.definitionCN: 小标记；小玩意儿（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: a tree of the same family with a rich edible nut and dark wood
entries.definitionCN: 胡桃；与山核桃同科的树，坚果美味、木材深色

entries.definition: a large tree with very hard wood, often used for tools and furniture
entries.definitionCN: 橡树；木质坚硬，常用作工具与家具材料

entries.definition: wood prepared for building or making things
entries.definitionCN: 木材；原木

normalIntro.en: Hickory is an Algonquian loanword for a tough American tree, so picture hardness whenever the word appears.
normalIntro.cn: hickory 是来自阿尔冈昆语的借词，指一种坚韧的北美树木，看到它就想「硬」。

normal.en: Use the plural hickories for several trees or pieces of wood.
normal.cn: 指多棵树或多块木材时用复数 hickories。

normal.en: The compound hickory nut works like other nut names such as walnut and chestnut.
normal.cn: 复合词 hickory nut 的构词方式与 walnut、chestnut 等坚果名相同。

normal.en: The adjective use is fixed in pairs like hickory handle and hickory-smoked.
normal.cn: 作形容词时多见于 hickory handle 与 hickory-smoked 这类固定搭配。

normal.en: Remember that the early spelling pohickory kept the original loanword shape.
normal.cn: 记住早期拼写 pohickory 保留了借词的原貌。

normal.en: Compare pecan: it is a nut of the same family, so both belong together in a nut vocabulary.
normal.cn: 对比 pecan：它也是同科坚果，两者可放在同一组坚果词汇里记。

abstract.en: Tap a hickory axe handle and hear how solid it sounds.
abstract.cn: 敲一敲山核桃木斧柄，听听那声音有多结实。

abstract.en: Picture a baseball bat splitting the air at the plate.
abstract.cn: 想象球棒在击球区划破空气。

abstract.en: Smell the sweet sharp smoke drifting from a barbecue pit.
abstract.cn: 想象烧烤炉里飘出的那股又甜又浓的烟味。

examples.en: Hickory trees line the old lane behind the barn.
examples.cn: 谷仓后面那条旧小路两旁长满了山核桃树。

examples.en: The carpenter chose hickory for the handles because it rarely splits.
examples.cn: 木匠选山核桃木做手柄，因为它很少开裂。

examples.en: This sauce is hickory smoked and tastes faintly of wood fire.
examples.cn: 这款酱是用山核桃木熏制的，带一点柴火的香味。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「嘿，可（硬）」——这木头硬得让人一敲就喊「嘿，可真硬」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 阿尔冈昆诸语中表示「捣碎坚果」或其木材的词 → 殖民时期借入英语，写作 pohickory、hiccory 等 → 十八世纪定型为 hickory。核心义「坚硬耐用的北美硬木」。

sensesIntro.en: Hickory starts as the tree and its nuts, passes to the timber cut from it, and finally to the smoke of that timber burning.
sensesIntro.cn: hickory 从这种树和它的坚果出发，转到取自它的木材，最后落到燃烧这种木材产生的烟熏味。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hard hickory axe handle that seems impossible to split.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根硬得几乎劈不开的山核桃木斧柄。

branches.en: The tree and its nuts are the botanical sense.
branches.cn: 树与坚果是植物学义项。

branches.en: The hard timber used for tools is the material sense.
branches.cn: 做工具的硬木材是材料义项。

branches.en: Smoke from burning the wood is the food sense.
branches.cn: 燃烧木材生出的烟是饮食义项。

branches.en: The tree and its timber share a single name because the wood is cut from that very tree.
branches.cn: 树与木材异名同源，因为木材正是从这种树上砍下来的。

branches.en: Burning the hard wood yields the strong sweet smoke.
branches.cn: 这种硬木燃烧后会产生浓郁带甜的烟。

intro.en: Hickory is a borrowing, not a built word; English shapes it with the -y ending and extends it through compounds such as hickory nut.
intro.cn: hickory 是借词而非用词缀构成；英语以 -y 收尾定型，并通过 hickory nut 这类复合词扩展。

latinIntro.en: The word has no Latin ancestor; the tree is called Carya in botanical Latin, a name taken from the Greek word for walnut.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语祖形；植物学拉丁语把山核桃属称为 Carya，该名取自希腊语中的「胡桃」。

items.meaning: an early colonial name for the nut
items.meaningCN: 殖民时期对这种坚果的早期称呼
items.example: Pohickory is the oldest recorded form.
items.exampleCN: pohickory 是文献中最早的写法。

items.meaning: an older spelling of the tree name
items.example: Hiccory appears in seventeenth century texts.
items.exampleCN: 十七世纪的文本里出现 hiccory。

items.meaning: the tree, its wood, or its nut
items.example: Hickory is the settled modern form.
items.exampleCN: hickory 是定型的现代写法。

items.meaning: closing element carried over from the loanword
items.meaningCN: 借词带过来的收尾成分
items.example: The ending -ry in hickory is not a living suffix.
items.exampleCN: hickory 中的 -ry 并非现役词缀。

items.example: Hickories keeps the consonant before -ies.
items.exampleCN: hickories 在 -ies 前保留辅音字母。

items.example: Hickory nut is a common compound.
items.exampleCN: hickory nut 是常见复合词。

items.example: Hickory smoked forms a compound adjective with a hyphen.
items.exampleCN: hickory 与 smoked 用连字符构成复合形容词。

items.example: Nut is paired with the tree name in the compound.
items.exampleCN: nut 在复合词中与树名搭配。

latinEntries.meaning: the genus of hickories and pecans

definition_zh: 远足；徒步；把物价或工资大幅提高；大幅上涨；徒步带着背包走
definition_en: to walk a long way in the countryside for pleasure, or a sharp rise in prices or rates
core_image: 背着小包沿野外小路一步步上行，走到高处回头看山谷
scene: 周末一群朋友背上水壶和地图，沿着山脊小路一步步往上走。At the weekend, a group of friends walked up the mountain path for a long hike.
sceneCN: 这里 hike 是「远足」（第 1 个义项：在乡间为了玩乐而长途步行）；句意：周末一群朋友沿着山间小路做了一次长长的远足。

derivatives.zh: 远足者；徒步旅行者
徒步运动
hike 的过去式与过去分词，义为「徒步走了；抬高了」

senses.title: To walk a long way in the countryside
senses.definition: to walk a long distance, especially across hills or countryside, for pleasure or exercise
senses.definitionCN: 为了玩乐或锻炼而长途步行，尤指在山野乡间走
senses.example: We hiked across the hills for six hours.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在山上徒步走了六个小时。
senses.why: The core image of lifting the foot and moving away by land grew into the idea of covering a long country path on foot.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是「抬脚上路、一路走」，于是长出「在乡间小路长途步行」这一义；从步行的动作到整段路程，画面一直延续。

senses.title: A long walk in nature
senses.definition: a long walk in the countryside, hills, or mountains, often taken for pleasure
senses.definitionCN: 在乡间、丘陵或山区进行的长途步行，常以游乐为目的
senses.example: The hike took us to the top of the ridge.
senses.exampleCN: 这次远足把我们带到了山脊顶端。
senses.why: The action turned into a countable noun, so one long country walk became a hike.
senses.whyCN: 动作本身转成可数名词，一次乡间长走就成了「一次远足」；这与从动词长出名词语义的常见路径一致。

senses.title: To raise prices or wages sharply
senses.definition: to increase a price, rate, or amount, often sharply and suddenly
senses.definitionCN: 把价格、费率或数量大幅且突然地提高
senses.example: The shop hiked its prices overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店一夜之间大幅提高了价格。
senses.why: A sudden sharp climb in numbers is imagined like a steep path going up, so raising a price is hiking it.
senses.whyCN: 数字突然陡升，就像走上一条陡坡，于是「抬价」被说成 hike；上行的画面从山路上搬到了价格上。

senses.title: A sharp rise in a rate
senses.definition: a sudden large increase in prices, taxes, or rates
senses.definitionCN: 价格、税收或费率突然的大幅上升
senses.example: The fuel hike angered many drivers.
senses.exampleCN: 油价大幅上涨让许多司机很生气。
senses.why: The noun branch extends to news language, where a jump in numbers is called a hike.
senses.whyCN: 名词语义继续扩展到新闻语体中，数字突然跳升便被称为 hike；画面里那条上坡路变成了曲线图上的陡升。

senses.title: To make a journey on foot with supplies
senses.definition: to travel on foot over a distance, usually carrying a pack and staying out for a while
senses.definitionCN: 背着行囊作一段距离的步行，通常在外过一段时间
senses.example: They hiked from the village to the lake in two days.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用两天从村庄徒步走到湖边。
senses.why: The verb widens from a short country walk to any long journey on foot with supplies.
senses.whyCN: 动词从乡间短途扩展到带补给的长途行走；核心画面仍是「一路走远」，只是时间和距离被拉长了。

intro.en: Hike is probably an English word of uncertain origin, first meaning to lift or hitch, then a long walk.
intro.cn: hike 大概源自英语本土词，词根来源不确定；早期义为「提起、拽高」，后来才有「长途步行」的意思。

items.en: The root is not settled; most dictionaries consider the early source uncertain.
items.cn: 词根来源不确定，多数词典认为早期来源无法确证。

items.en: Early hike meant to lift something up or pull it with a jerk.
items.cn: 较早的 hike 义为「把东西提起」或「猛地一拽」。

items.en: The sense grew into a long walk or tramp across country.
items.cn: 十九世纪，词义扩展为乡间的长途步行或漫游。

items.en: American usage took hike as a brisk journey on foot.
items.cn: 美式英语把 hike 用作轻快走路、徒步。

items.en: Hike also names a sudden rise in prices or wages.
items.cn: 二十世纪又引申出「价格或工资的大幅上涨」。

note.en: Hike sits near hiker, hiking, and trail words, and close to walk, trek, and stroll.
note.cn: hike 与 hiker、hiking 同属「徒步」词族，并在语义上靠近 walk、trek、stroll。

entries.definition: a person who hikes
entries.definitionCN: 远足者；徒步者

entries.definition: the activity of hiking
entries.definitionCN: 徒步运动

entries.definition: to fasten or catch on something
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写相近，词源与 hike 不同，并不同源

entries.definition: to move along on foot
