entries.definitionCN: 步行；走路

entries.definition: a long hard walk
entries.definitionCN: 艰苦的长途跋涉

entries.definition: to walk slowly and easily
entries.definitionCN: 悠闲散步

normalIntro.en: Hike pictures a foot lifting up and going out along a country path.
normalIntro.cn: hike 让人看见一只脚抬起，沿着乡间小路一路走远。

normal.en: Go hiking means setting off for a walk in the hills.
normal.cn: go hiking 就是出发去山间徒步。

normal.en: A price hike is an upward jump, as if prices had walked up a slope.
normal.cn: price hike 是价格的跳升，就像价格走上了一道坡。

normal.en: The person is a hiker, the activity is hiking.
normal.cn: 人叫 hiker，活动叫 hiking。

normal.en: Compare walk, hike, and trek from short to long and hard.
normal.cn: 对比 walk、hike 与 trek，强度依次从小闲走到长途跋涉。

normal.en: Note that a hike is countable: go for a hike.
normal.cn: hike 可数，常搭配 go for a hike。

abstract.en: Picture boots lifting one after another on a winding trail.
abstract.cn: 想象登山靴在蜿蜒小径上一前一后抬起。

abstract.en: Think of a path end, where you look back at the valley you crossed.
abstract.cn: 想象小路尽头，你回头望着刚走过的山谷。

abstract.en: See a price chart rising steeply like a mountain slope.
abstract.cn: 想象一张价格图像山坡一样陡峭上升。

examples.en: We hiked to the waterfall along the valley.
examples.cn: 我们沿河谷徒步走到瀑布。

examples.en: The railway announced a ticket price hike.
examples.cn: 铁路公司宣布票价上涨。

examples.en: The museum plans to hike admission charges next year.
examples.cn: 博物馆计划明年提高门票费用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「海客」——一位来自海外的客人沿着山路走，就是徒步远足；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语本土词，词根来源不确定；早期义「提起、拽高」→「乡间长途步行」→「价格陡升」，核心义「抬脚上路、走高」。

sensesIntro.en: Hike starts as a long country walk, becomes a countable outing, then a sharp rise in numbers.
sensesIntro.cn: hike 先指乡间长途步行，再指一次远足，最后扩展到数字的大幅上升。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a foot lifts and carries a walker up a country path.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只脚抬起，带着徒步者沿乡间小路上行。

branches.en: The walking verb is the base sense.
branches.cn: 步行动词是基础义项。

branches.en: The counted walk is the noun outing.
branches.cn: 可数的那次长走是「远足」名词义。

branches.en: Raising a price mirrors walking up a slope.
branches.cn: 抬价就像走上坡路。

branches.en: The noun branch extends to a jump in rates.
branches.cn: 名词语义延伸到费率跳升。

branches.en: Both an outing and a supply journey are long walks on foot.
branches.cn: 远足与背包长途都是靠双脚走过的长路。

intro.en: Hike is a short English word; its family grows with the suffix -er and the gerund -ing.
intro.cn: hike 是简短的英语词，词族靠后缀 -er（表示人）和 -ing（表示活动）扩展。

latinIntro.en: Hike has no accepted Latin source, so there are no Latin cognates to list.
latinIntro.cn: hike 没有公认的拉丁语来源，因此没有可列出的拉丁同源词。

items.example: Hike is the base form of the family.
items.exampleCN: hike 是这个词族的基础形式。

items.example: Hike also works as a countable noun.
items.exampleCN: hike 也可作可数名词。

items.example: She hikes every summer.
items.exampleCN: 她每年夏天都去远足。

items.example: They hiked all day.
items.exampleCN: 他们走了一整天。

items.example: Hiking is popular in the hills.
items.exampleCN: 在山区徒步很受欢迎。

items.example: A hiker carried a heavy pack.
items.exampleCN: 一位徒步者背着沉重的包。

items.example: The suffix -er forms hiker from hike.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 把 hike 变成 hiker。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms hiking.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 hiking。

items.example: They hiked up the rent.
items.exampleCN: 他们大幅提高了租金。

items.example: A price hike hurt small shops.
items.exampleCN: 物价上涨伤害了小商铺。

definition_zh: 极其好笑的；令人捧腹的；很滑稽的；明快爽朗的（古旧义）
definition_en: extremely funny and causing a lot of laughter
core_image: 满屋的人笑得前仰后合，眼泪都笑出来了
scene: 一段短视频让办公室所有人笑到拍桌子，眼泪都出来了。The short video was so hilarious that everyone in the office laughed until they cried.
sceneCN: 这里 hilarious 是「极其好笑的」（第 1 个义项：好笑得让人放声大笑）；句意：这段短视频太好笑了，办公室里每个人都笑到流泪。

pos.zh: 极其好笑的；令人捧腹的

derivatives.zh: 欢闹；兴高采烈
极其好笑地

senses.title: Extremely funny
senses.definition: very funny, and making people laugh loudly
senses.definitionCN: 非常好笑，能让人放声大笑
senses.example: The comedy was hilarious from start to finish.
senses.exampleCN: 这部喜剧从头到尾都极其好笑。
senses.why: The Latin root points to cheerful or merry, so hilarious reaches the top of a scale of funniness.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根指向「欢快、喜悦」，所以 hilarious 落在「好笑」这个程度尺度的顶端；从欢快的情绪到让人大笑，义项顺着同一条情绪线长出来。

senses.title: Causing loud laughter
senses.definition: so funny that it produces an outburst of laughing
senses.definitionCN: 好笑到让人忍不住爆发出笑声
senses.example: His hilarious impersonation made the room roar.
senses.exampleCN: 他那令人捧腹的模仿让全场哈哈大笑。
senses.why: Hilarious can also describe a thing, a person, or a situation as a trigger of laughter.
senses.whyCN: hilarious 不只形容好笑，也能形容引发笑声的对象，如笑话、人和场面；义项从「感受好笑」扩到「成为笑声的来源」。

senses.title: Ridiculous or absurd
senses.definition: so silly or ridiculous that it seems funny
senses.definitionCN: 因为太荒唐而显得滑稽可笑
senses.example: The regulation is hilarious in its own odd logic.
senses.exampleCN: 这条规定按它自己的古怪逻辑显得滑稽可笑。
senses.why: Something absurd can look funny, so hilarious also shades into silliness and mockery.
senses.whyCN: 荒唐的事常常自带笑点，hilarious 因此也带上「荒谬得可笑」的意味，可用来调侃；这种用法保留了「看出滑稽」的核心。

senses.title: Cheerful and merry
senses.definition: lightly cheerful or merry, now mainly a literary and rare use
senses.definitionCN: 轻松欢快、心情舒畅，现在主要用于文学语体，较为罕见
senses.example: The old poem calls the season a hilarious one.
senses.exampleCN: 那首古诗把这一季节称为欢快的时光。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply cheerful, without any laughter, and it survives only in literary writing.
senses.whyCN: 最早的义项只是「欢快」，并不涉及听众发笑；这个义项如今只残留在文学笔调里，是核心情绪意象最本源的样子。

senses.title: Very funny in a warm way
senses.definition: bringing laughter together with a light, friendly feeling
senses.definitionCN: 带来笑声的同时还带出轻松友好的氛围
senses.example: Their hilarious banter kept the whole table smiling.
senses.exampleCN: 他们那段好笑又温暖的打趣让整桌人一直笑着。
senses.why: Because the root carries cheer, hilarious often suggests fond laughter rather than contempt.
senses.whyCN: 词根带「喜悦、欢快」色彩，所以 hilarious 常指充满好感的笑，而不是嘲笑；这正体现了欢快这一底层意象。

intro.en: Hilarious comes from Latin hilaris and hilarus, cheerful, which come from Greek hilaros, merry.
intro.cn: hilarious 来自拉丁语 hilaris 与 hilarus（欢快的），它们的源头是希腊语 hilaros（快乐、明朗）。

items.en: Hilaros means cheerful, merry, and glad.
items.cn: 希腊语 hilaros 意为欢快、愉快、明朗。

items.en: The word is linked to hilaos, meaning gracious or mild.
items.cn: 这个词被认为与 hilaos（和善、温和）相关。

items.en: Latin hilaris and hilarus carry the cheerful sense into the language.
items.cn: 拉丁语 hilaris 与 hilarus 把这个「欢快」义带入拉丁语。

items.en: Hilarious first meant cheerful or merry in English.
items.cn: 十七世纪进入英语时，hilarious 义为「欢快的、愉快的」。

items.en: The meaning shifted toward extremely funny and causing laughter.
items.cn: 现代英语中词义转向「极其好笑、引人发笑」。

note.en: Hilarious keeps the cheerful root of hilarity, and it sits beside funny, amusing, and comical.
note.cn: hilarious 保留了 hilarity 中「欢快」的词根，并在语义上靠近 funny、amusing 与 comical。

entries.definition: great merriment and laughter
entries.definitionCN: 欢闹；一片笑声

entries.definition: in a very funny way
entries.definitionCN: 极其好笑地

entries.definition: the quality of being hilarious
entries.definitionCN: 极其好笑的性质

entries.definition: causing laughter
entries.definitionCN: 好笑的；有趣的

entries.definition: entertaining and mildly funny
entries.definitionCN: 好玩的；有趣而令人发笑的

entries.definition: funny in a strange or silly way
entries.definitionCN: 滑稽的；怪得好笑的

normalIntro.en: Hilarious grows from a Latin root for cheerful, and the -ous ending marks it as an adjective.
normalIntro.cn: hilarious 长自表示「欢快」的拉丁词根，词尾 -ous 表明它是形容词。

normal.en: Hilarious is stronger than funny, like a five-star funniness.
normal.cn: hilarious 比 funny 更强烈，相当于「五星级」的好笑。

normal.en: The noun hilarity means lively laughter.
normal.cn: 名词 hilarity 表示热闹的欢笑声。

normal.en: Use absolutely hilarious to stress the extreme degree.
normal.cn: 用 absolutely hilarious 强调极高的程度。

normal.en: The -ous ending means full of, as in joyous.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ous 意为「充满……的」，如 joyous。

normal.en: Compare amusing and hilarious: amusing is mild, hilarious is loud and extreme.
normal.cn: 对比 amusing 与 hilarious：前者温和，后者夸张、让人大笑。

abstract.en: Picture a room where everyone is bent over with laughter.
abstract.cn: 想象一屋子人笑得直不起腰。

abstract.en: Picture tears of laughter running down a face.
abstract.cn: 想象笑出来的眼泪顺着脸颊往下流。

abstract.en: Picture a joke that gets the whole crowd roaring at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一个笑话让全场同时哄笑。

examples.en: The clown act was hilarious and the children could not stop giggling.
examples.cn: 小丑表演极其好笑，孩子们笑个不停。

examples.en: She told a hilarious story about her first day at work.
examples.cn: 她讲了一个关于第一天上班的极其好笑的故事。

examples.en: I found the mix of accents hilarious.
examples.cn: 我觉得几种口音混在一起实在是太好笑了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「嘿笑」——听到好笑的话就先「嘿」地笑出声，就是极其好笑；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 hilaros（欢快、明朗），与 hilaos（和善）相关 → 拉丁语 hilarus / hilaris（欢快的）→ 英语 hilarious，核心义「欢快」→「好笑得让人大笑」。

sensesIntro.en: Hilarious begins with cheer, then moves to extreme funniness, then to absurdity.
sensesIntro.cn: hilarious 从「欢快」出发，发展为「极其好笑」，再延伸到「荒唐可笑」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: people bent over with laughter and tears in their eyes.
core.cn: 核心意象：满屋的人笑得前仰后合，眼里都是笑出来的泪。

branches.en: The extreme funniness sense is the everyday one.
branches.cn: 「极其好笑」是日常主用义。

branches.en: A thing that triggers laughter is also called hilarious.
branches.cn: 引发笑声的事物也叫 hilarious。

branches.en: Absurdity adds a mocking shade.
branches.cn: 荒谬带来调侃色彩。

branches.en: The older cheerful sense survives in writing.
branches.cn: 较早的欢快义残留在书面语中。

branches.en: Warm laughter links the extreme and the friendly uses.
branches.cn: 温暖的笑把「极其好笑」与「好笑又温暖」连在一起。

intro.en: Hilarious is built from the root hilar and the suffix -ous, with the family noun hilarity.
intro.cn: hilarious 由词根 hilar 加后缀 -ous 构成，词族中还有名词 hilarity。

latinIntro.en: Latin hilaris and hilarus mean cheerful, and both trace back to Greek hilaros.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 hilaris 与 hilarus 意为「欢快的」，二者都追溯到希腊语 hilaros。

items.example: The root hilar carries the idea of cheer.
items.exampleCN: 词根 hilar 承载「欢快」的含义。

items.example: The suffix -ous forms hilarious.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ous 构成 hilarious。

items.example: Hilarious describes something that makes people roar.
items.exampleCN: hilarious 形容让人放声大笑的事物。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms hilarity.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 构成 hilarity。

items.example: Hilarity filled the hall.
items.exampleCN: 大厅里一片欢闹。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms hilariously.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 hilariously。

items.example: He acted hilariously on stage.
items.exampleCN: 他在台上演得极其好笑。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms hilariousness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 hilariousness。

items.meaning: the quality of being extremely funny
items.example: Hilariousness is rare in scripts.
items.exampleCN: 剧本中真正好笑的作品很少。

definition_zh: 铰链；合页；关键所在；取决于；靠铰链转动
definition_en: a metal piece that joins a door to its frame and lets it swing open and shut
core_image: 门轴上的一小块金属，门板绕着它开合
scene: 旧木门歪斜了，原来是上面的合页松了，门板再也关不严。The old wooden door sagged because the top hinge had come loose.
sceneCN: 这里 hinge 是「合页、铰链」（第 1 个义项：连接门与门框、让门能开合的金属件）；句意：这扇旧木门下垂了，因为上面的合页松了。

collocations.phrase: lift the door off its hinges

derivatives.zh: 带铰链的；可打开的
脱轴的；精神失常的

senses.title: A joint that lets a door swing
senses.definition: a piece of metal or other material that joins two parts, such as a door and its frame, and lets one part turn
senses.definitionCN: 连接门与门框等两个部件、并让其中一个能转动的金属或其它材料制的连接件
senses.example: The door swung on a rusty hinge.
senses.exampleCN: 那扇门靠一根生锈的铰链开合。
senses.why: The core image is the metal eye that a pin slides through, the physical pivot of the door.
senses.whyCN: 核心画面就是穿轴的小金属环，是门板真正的支点；铰链这个实物直接对应这条意象，一点也没有引申。

senses.title: To depend on
senses.definition: to depend entirely on something, especially a decision or event
senses.definitionCN: 完全依赖于某事物，尤指某个决定或事件
senses.example: Everything hinges on tomorrow and its result.
senses.exampleCN: 一切都取决于明天和它的结果。
senses.why: A door hangs on its hinge, so depending on something is imagined as hanging from it.
senses.whyCN: 门靠铰链挂着，所以「依赖某事」被想象成「挂在它上面」；从门的物理支点到事情的支点，转喻一路延伸。

senses.title: The crucial point
senses.definition: the central point on which a situation or argument turns
senses.definitionCN: 局势或论证所依赖、转折的核心点
senses.example: That question was the hinge of the debate.
senses.exampleCN: 那个问题是这场辩论的关键。
senses.why: The noun moves from the physical pivot to a turning point in events, the point everything turns around.
senses.whyCN: 名词从实物的转轴转到事件的转折点；门绕轴转动，事情也绕「关键」转向，画面被类比着搬进了抽象领域。

senses.title: To be attached by a hinge
senses.definition: to be attached to something so that it can turn, or to supply something with a hinge
senses.definitionCN: 被装成可以转动的连接，或给某物装上铰链
senses.example: The lid is hinged at the back.
senses.exampleCN: 盖子在后侧用铰链连接。
senses.why: The noun became a verb describing how a part is fixed so that it turns.
senses.whyCN: 名词转成动词，表示某部件被装成能转动的样子；这条义项是把实物的「连接方式」动作化了。

senses.title: A turnabout in a process
senses.definition: a point in a process or story where things turn toward a new direction
senses.definitionCN: 过程或故事中事情转向新方向的那一点
senses.example: The meeting proved to be the hinge of events.
senses.exampleCN: 这场会议被证明是事件的转折点。
senses.why: From the mechanical turning point comes the abstract idea of a moment when a story turns.
senses.whyCN: 从机械意义上的转轴引申出「故事转向的那一刻」；凡事总要绕着某个点转弯，抽象的转折点由此长出。

intro.en: Hinge comes from Middle English henge, related to the verb hang, so its root image is something hanging.
intro.cn: hinge 来自中古英语 henge，与动词 hang（悬挂）同源，词根的意象是「挂着的」。

items.en: A reconstructed Germanic root connected with hanging lies behind the word.
items.cn: 一般认为其背后是一个与「悬挂」相关的日耳曼语重构词根。

items.en: Henge appears as a hinge or hanging object.
items.cn: 中古英语 henge 表示铰链或悬挂之物。

items.en: Hinge is recorded in writing for the joint of a door.
items.cn: 铰链义在十四五世纪已有书面记录。

items.en: The phrase hinge upon appears for depending on something.
items.cn: 十七世纪出现 hinge upon 的用法，表示「取决于」。

items.en: Hinge expands into figurative words for key moments.
items.cn: 现代英语把 hinge 扩展为表示关键时刻的抽象说法。

items.en: Hinged devices and the word unhinged join the family.
items.cn: 二十世纪，带铰链的装置以及派生的 unhinged 加入词族。

note.en: Hinge is a hanging joint; it is related to hinged and unhinged, and it lives near pivot and joint words.
note.cn: hinge 是「挂着转动的关节」，与 hinged、unhinged 同族，语义上靠近 pivot、joint 一类表示支点的词。

entries.definition: fitted with a hinge
entries.definitionCN: 带铰链的；可开合的

entries.definition: taken off its hinges or mentally unbalanced
entries.definitionCN: 脱轴的；精神失常的

entries.definition: a prehistoric ring of stones such as Stonehenge
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写相近，词源不同；henge 指史前石圈

entries.definition: a central point on which something turns
entries.definitionCN: 支点；中心

entries.definition: a place where two parts are connected
entries.definitionCN: 关节；接合处

entries.definition: to be decided by something else
entries.definitionCN: 取决于；依赖

normalIntro.en: Hinge is a hanging joint, and the phrase hinge on keeps the picture of a door hanging from it.
normalIntro.cn: hinge 是「挂着转动的关节」，短语 hinge on 保留了门「挂」在铰链上的画面。

normal.en: A hinge lets a door swing, so hinge on means to depend on.
normal.cn: 铰链让门转动，所以 hinge on 表示取决于。

normal.en: The un- prefix in unhinged means off, as in off the hinges.
normal.cn: unhinged 中的前缀 un- 表示「脱离」，即「脱开铰链」。

normal.en: Hinged records and hinged boxes open at the hinge.
normal.cn: 带铰链的记录本和盒子都在铰链处打开。

normal.en: Compare hinge and pivot: both turn, but a hinge is fixed to an edge.
normal.cn: 对比 hinge 与 pivot：都能转动，但 hinge 固定在一条边上。

normal.en: Doors, lids, and laptop screens all use hinges.
normal.cn: 门、盖子以及笔记本电脑屏幕都用铰链。

abstract.en: Picture a door swinging quietly on two worn hinges.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门在两只磨旧的铰链上无声开合。

abstract.en: Picture a lid lifting up from its back hinge.
abstract.cn: 想象一个盖子从后侧铰链向上翻开。

abstract.en: Picture a whole plan hanging from one small metal pin.
abstract.cn: 想象整个计划都挂在一根小小的金属轴上。

examples.en: Fix the loose hinge before the door falls.
examples.cn: 趁门还没掉下来，先把松动的铰链修好。

examples.en: The outcome hinges on whether the vote passes.
examples.cn: 结果取决于投票能否通过。

examples.en: The gate swung on silent hinges.
examples.cn: 大门在无声的铰链上转动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「金记」——门轴上的这块小金件，把门和门框「记」在一起，这就是合页；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 一般认为源自与中古英语 henge（挂、铰链）相关的日耳曼语词根，与 hang（悬挂）同源 → 英语 hinge，核心义「悬挂着转动的关节」→ 引申为「取决于」。

sensesIntro.en: Hinge starts as the joint a door turns on, then becomes the act of depending, then the idea of a key point.
sensesIntro.cn: hinge 先指门绕之转动的铰链，再转为「取决于」，最后成为「关键、转折点」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small metal hinge around which a door swings.
core.cn: 核心意象：门能开合，靠的是绕着一小块金属铰链转。

branches.en: The metal joint is the literal sense.
branches.cn: 金属关节是字面义项。

branches.en: Depending on is the hanging image applied to plans.
branches.cn: 取决于是把「悬挂」意象用到计划上。

branches.en: A key point is the fixed pivot in an argument.
branches.cn: 关键点是论证中的那个支点。

branches.en: The verb describes the fitting itself.
branches.cn: 动词描述的是连接方式本身。

branches.en: Both key points and turning points are places where things turn.
branches.cn: 关键点与转折点都是事情转弯的地方。

intro.en: Hinge is a short English word; the family grows with the un- prefix and the -ed ending.
intro.cn: hinge 是简短的英语词，词族靠前缀 un-（表示脱离）和词尾 -ed 扩展。

latinIntro.en: Hinge has no Latin origin, since its root is Germanic, so there are no Latin cognates to list.
latinIntro.cn: hinge 的词根属日耳曼语系，没有拉丁语来源，因此没有可列出的拉丁同源词。

items.meaning: a joint that lets a door turn
items.example: Hinge is the base word.
items.exampleCN: hinge 是基础词。

items.example: Everything hinges on this choice.
items.exampleCN: 一切都取决于这个选择。

items.example: A hinged lid covered the box.
items.exampleCN: 一个带铰链的盖子盖住了盒子。

items.example: The plan is hinging on one vote.
items.exampleCN: 这一计划系于一张选票。

items.example: The door came un- off its hinges.
items.exampleCN: 这门从铰链上脱了下来。

items.meaning: taken off the hinges, or mentally unsettled
items.example: The gate stood unhinged after the storm.
items.exampleCN: 风暴过后大门脱了轴。

items.example: Their success hinges on timing.
items.exampleCN: 他们的成功取决于时机。

items.example: The suffix -ed turns hinge into hinged.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 把 hinge 变成 hinged。

items.example: A door hinge creaked.
items.exampleCN: 一根门铰链嘎吱作响。

definition_zh: 内陆；腹地；内地；港口或城市背后的广大地区；（国家或城市背后的）经济腹地
definition_en: the land that lies behind a coast, port, or city, especially the area that supplies or depends on it
core_image: 从海岸线往内陆望去，一片土地在港口身后一直铺到山脉脚下
scene: 一张沿海地图上，港口背后的大片陆地被涂成了同一种颜色。The port grew rich by trading with the fertile hinterland behind it.
sceneCN: 这里 hinterland 是「腹地、内地」（第 1 个义项：港口或城市背后、为其提供供给的广大内陆地区）；句意：这个港口靠着与身后富饶的腹地做生意而富起来。

pos.zh: 经济腹地；周边地区（城市或机构的辐射范围）

derivatives.zh: hinterland 加复数词尾 -s 构成，指多个彼此相邻的腹地地区，常见于 hinterlands of Africa 一类说法
德语 hinter（后面）借入英语构词层的罕用成分，只在 hinterland 等少数词里露面，义为「后面的」
由 fore-（前）+ land（土地）构成，与 hinterland 前呼后应，义为「前滩地、海角前方的陆地」

senses.title: The land behind a coast or port
senses.definition: the area of country that lies inland behind a coast, port, or city and supplies it with goods and people
senses.definitionCN: 位于海岸、港口或城市背后、为其提供货物与人口的广大内陆地区
senses.example: Farm produce flows from the hinterland to the port.
senses.exampleCN: 农产品从腹地流向港口。
senses.why: German hinter means behind, so the hinterland is literally the land lying behind the coast or port.
senses.whyCN: 德语 hinter 意为「后面」，所以腹地字面上就是海岸或港口背后那片土地，这是该词最早也是最稳的义项。

senses.title: The inland parts of a country
senses.definition: the far inland regions of a country, often less developed or remote from the capital and the coast
senses.definitionCN: 一个国家遥远的内陆地区，往往较不发达，或远离首都与海岸
senses.example: Traders carried salt from the coast to the hinterland.
senses.exampleCN: 商人把盐从沿海运往内陆。
senses.why: Once the word names land behind a coast, it slides to the whole inland interior, seen from the viewpoint of the capital and the sea.
senses.whyCN: 一旦它指「沿海背后之地」，就会顺势泛指整片内陆，因为地理学家习惯从首都与海洋的视角来划分国土。

senses.title: The economic catchment of a city
senses.definition: the surrounding region whose trade, labour, and produce are drawn on by a city, port, or institution
senses.definitionCN: 为某一城市、港口或机构提供贸易、劳动力与产品的周边地区
senses.example: The university draws students from a wide hinterland.
senses.exampleCN: 这所大学从一大片周边地区招收学生。
senses.why: Ports and cities survive on what the land behind them sends, so hinterland became an economic word for a catchment area.
senses.whyCN: 港口与城市靠身后土地送来的东西生存，因此 hinterland 自然从地理词变成表示「供给范围」的经济词。

senses.title: A neglected cultural backwater
senses.titleCN: 文化落后的地方；边缘地带
senses.definition: figurative use for a place or sphere that is seen as provincial, neglected, or far from the main centre of activity
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，指被视为偏僻、落后或远离主要活动中心的某个地方或领域
senses.example: Some call the old fishing town a cultural hinterland.
senses.exampleCN: 有人把这个旧渔镇称为文化上的边远地带。
senses.why: Because hinterlands are often poorer and quieter than the coast, the word borrows a hint of neglect when applied to culture.
senses.whyCN: 腹地往往比沿海贫穷安静，所以当它用来谈文化时，就带上了一点「被遗忘的偏远角落」的色彩。

intro.en: Hinterland is a late nineteenth century borrowing from German, where hinter means behind and Land means land.
intro.cn: hinterland 是十九世纪后期从德语借入的词，德语 hinter 意为「后面」，land 即「土地」。

items.en: The word family behind hinter is related to English hinder and to Old High German hinter, meaning behind.
items.cn: hinter 所属的日耳曼词族与英语 hinder 同源，古高地德语 hinter 意为「在后面」。

items.en: German combines hinter and Land into Hinterland for the land that lies behind a coast or river.
items.cn: 德语把 hinter 与 Land 组合成 Hinterland，指海岸或河流背后的土地。

items.en: Geographers writing in German use the term for the inland area that feeds a port.
items.cn: 用德语写作的地理学家用这个词指为港口提供物资的内陆地区。

items.en: English borrows hinterland, often with report of German colonial trade and settlement.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪九十年代前后借入 hinterland，当时常与德国在非洲的殖民地贸易报道一同出现，确切首见年份存疑。

items.en: The word spreads from geography and trade to any area behind a centre of activity.
items.cn: 这个词从地理与贸易领域扩展到任何「活动中心背后的地方」。

items.en: Hinterland is used literally and figuratively, for inland regions and for cultural backwaters.
items.cn: 现代英语中 hinterland 既可实指内陆地区，也可比喻文化上的边缘地带。

note.en: Hinterland is the German land behind a coast, standing beside inland words and its own compounds.
note.cn: hinterland 是来自德语的「海岸背后的土地」，与表示内陆的近义词以及它自己的复合词相邻。

entries.definition: to get in the way of something
entries.definitionCN: 阻碍；妨碍（与 hinterland 的 hinter 同出「在后面」的日耳曼词根）

entries.definition: a piece of land in front of the coast
entries.definitionCN: 前滩地；海岸前方的陆地（fore- 与 hinter- 正好相对）

entries.definition: German for behind
entries.definitionCN: 德语「在后面」；land 之前的那个部分

entries.definition: the inner part of a country, away from the coast
entries.definitionCN: 内陆；国家的内部地区

entries.definition: remote country away from towns
entries.definitionCN: 偏远乡村；远离城镇的地区

entries.definition: the remote inland of Australia
entries.definitionCN: 澳大利亚的内陆荒野

normalIntro.en: Read hinterland as German behind plus land: everything that lies behind a coast or a port.
normalIntro.cn: 把 hinterland 读成德语「后面 + 土地」：凡是海岸或港口背后的地方，都算腹地。

normal.en: Hinter means behind, so the hinterland is the land behind the coast.
normal.cn: hinter 意为「后面」，所以腹地就是海岸背后的土地。

normal.en: In trade talk, a port and its hinterland are named together.
normal.cn: 谈贸易时，港口和它的腹地总被成对提起。

normal.en: The adjective rural often sits before hinterland, as in a rural hinterland.
normal.cn: 形容词 rural 常放在 hinterland 前，说成「乡村腹地」。

normal.en: Compare foreland: fore- is in front, hinter- is behind.
normal.cn: 对比 foreland：fore- 表示前面，hinter- 表示后面。

normal.en: Hinder and hinterland share the idea of something standing at the back.
normal.cn: hinder 与 hinterland 共享「处在后面」这一想法。

abstract.en: Picture a harbour with a whole countryside spread out behind it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个海港，身后铺开整片乡野。

abstract.en: Picture a railway line running inland from the docks into open fields.
abstract.cn: 想象一条铁路从码头伸进内陆的田野。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp in a city casting light over the towns around it.
abstract.cn: 想象城里的一盏灯，把光洒向周围的城镇。

examples.en: The railway links the port with its agricultural hinterland.
examples.cn: 这条铁路把港口与它的农业腹地连在一起。

examples.en: Many families moved from the coast into the hinterland after the floods.
examples.cn: 洪水之后，许多家庭从沿海搬进了内陆。

examples.en: The museum draws visitors from a wide hinterland.
examples.cn: 这座博物馆吸引了一大批周边地区的游客。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「 hinter 后面 + land 土地」——把土地的柜子门拉开，后面那一片就是腹地；这只是拆读联想，与正规词源表述略有简化，并非谐音造词。

root: 德语 hinter（后面）+ Land（土地）→ 德语 Hinterland（海岸或河流背后的土地）→ 十九世纪后期进入英语 hinterland，核心义「海岸与港口背后的大片内陆」。

sensesIntro.en: Hinterland begins as the land behind a coast, widens to the inland of a country, becomes the economic catchment of a city, and ends as a figure for a cultural backwater.
sensesIntro.cn: hinterland 先指海岸背后的土地，再扩大到一国的内陆，随后成为城市的经济腹地，最后引申为文化上的边缘地带。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wide stretch of land lying behind a port.
core.cn: 核心意象：港口背后铺展开的一大片土地。

branches.en: The land behind a coast or port is the core sense.
branches.cn: 海岸或港口背后的土地是核心义项。

branches.en: The whole inland interior is the wider geographic use.
branches.cn: 整片内陆是更宽的地理用法。

branches.en: The economic catchment of a city is the trade sense.
branches.cn: 城市的经济腹地是贸易义项。

branches.en: The cultural backwater is the figurative sense.
branches.cn: 文化边缘地带是比喻义项。

branches.en: A port and its hinterland form one economic unit.
branches.cn: 港口与腹地构成同一个经济单位。

intro.en: Hinterland is a Germanic compound, with hinter and land as its two halves and foreland as its mirrored partner.
intro.cn: hinterland 是日耳曼语系复合词，由 hinter 与 land 两半组成，与它相对的镜像词是 foreland。

latinIntro.en: Hinterland has no Latin element: both halves come from Germanic words for behind and land.
latinIntro.cn: hinterland 没有拉丁成分：前后两半都来自日耳曼语表示「后面」与「土地」的词。

items.example: Hinter supplies the behind of the word.
items.exampleCN: hinter 提供「后面」这个意思。

items.example: Land is the same word in German and English.
items.exampleCN: land 在德语和英语里是同一个词。

items.example: Hinterland splits into two simple halves.
items.exampleCN: Hinterland 可以拆成两个简单的部分。

items.example: Hinterlands names several regions at once.
items.exampleCN: hinterlands 一次指多个地区。

items.example: Fore- is the mirror of hinter.
items.exampleCN: fore- 与 hinter 正好相对。

items.meaning: land in front of the coast
items.meaningCN: 前滩地；海角前方的陆地
items.example: Foreland swaps the halves of hinterland.
items.exampleCN: foreland 把 hinterland 的两部分换了位置。

items.meaningCN: 表示土地、地区的构词成分
items.example: The element -land builds highland and farmland too.
items.exampleCN: 构词成分 -land 也构成 highland 与 farmland。

items.example: Hinder shares the behind sense of hinter.
items.exampleCN: hinder 与 hinter 共享「在后面」的含义。

items.example: Countryside is often the modern everyday partner of hinterland.
items.exampleCN: countryside 常是 hinterland 在今天的日常替身。

items.example: Back- carries the rear idea in backpack and backwater.
items.exampleCN: back- 在 backpack 与 backwater 中带有「后部」的意思。

definition_zh: 河马（hippopotamus 的口语简称）；「河马」式的人或物
definition_en: a very large African animal that lives in or near rivers, and is the short everyday name for the hippopotamus
core_image: 一头圆滚滚的灰色巨兽半沉在河里，只露出眼睛和耳朵，水面只到它背上
scene: 动物园的河马池边，游客隔着矮墙指着一团冒出水面的脊背。A hippo floated in the pool with only its eyes above the water.
sceneCN: 这里 hippo 是「河马」（第 1 个义项：生活在河边的非洲大型动物，hippopotamus 的日常简称）；句意：一头河马浮在池中，只有眼睛露出水面。

pos.zh: （比喻）又胖又笨重的人或东西

collocations.zh: 河马（与非洲草原生活相对）

derivatives.zh: 由希腊语 hippos（马）+ potamos（河流）构成的完整词，hippo 只是它口语中的缩短形式，义为「河马」
hippopotamus 的拉丁式复数，常见于书面与科普文章，义为「河马（复数）」
由希腊语 hippos（马）+ dromos（跑道）构成，共享「马」这一成分，义为「赛马场；马术表演场」

senses.title: The large river-dwelling animal
senses.definition: a huge greyish African mammal with a broad head and short legs that spends much of its day in rivers and lakes
senses.definitionCN: 一种灰蓝色的非洲大型哺乳动物，头宽腿短，白天大部分时间泡在河流与湖泊里
senses.example: A hippo can stay under water for several minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 一头河马能在水下待上好几分钟。
senses.why: Hippo is simply the clipped first half of hippopotamus, the Greek river horse, kept as the ordinary word.
senses.whyCN: hippo 只是 hippopotamus（希腊语「河中之马」）被截下来的前半段，作为日常口语保留下来，这是最常用的义项。

senses.title: The word as a nickname
senses.definition: a friendly or teasing nickname for a heavy, slow-moving person or a big clumsy vehicle
senses.definitionCN: 对胖而行动迟缓的人，或对笨重的大车子的亲昵或调侃式称呼
senses.example: His mates call the heavy old bus the hippo.
senses.exampleCN: 伙伴们把那辆笨重的旧巴士叫作「河马」。
senses.why: Big body, short legs, and a slow waddle make the hippo a natural nickname for anything heavy and ungainly.
senses.whyCN: 身躯硕大、腿又短、走路慢悠悠，这让河马成为一切笨重之物天然的绰号。

senses.title: The hippo of legend
senses.definition: the hippopotamus as a figure in ancient Egyptian religion, where a female hippo-shaped goddess protected mothers and children
senses.definitionCN: 古代尼罗河流域的人们视河马为凶险的猛兽，又在宗教中赋予它神圣地位，雌河马形的女神尤其护佑孕产
senses.example: Ancient painters carved a hippo into the tomb wall.
senses.exampleCN: 古代的工匠把一头河马刻进了墓壁。
senses.why: To people who lived by the Nile the animal was both a danger and a guardian, so it entered art and religion early.
senses.whyCN: 对生活在尼罗河边的人来说，河马既是威胁也是守护者，所以它最早进入了艺术与神话，成为带神圣色彩的形象。

intro.en: Hippo is clipped from hippopotamus, a Greek name meaning river horse, taken into Latin and then English in the fourteenth century.
intro.cn: hippo 由 hippopotamus 截短而来；hippopotamus 是希腊语名，意为「河中之马」，经拉丁语于十四世纪进入英语。

items.en: Hippos means horse and potamos means river, giving hippopotamos, the river horse.
items.cn: 希腊语 hippos 意为「马」，potamos 意为「河流」，合起来就是「河中之马」。

items.en: Latin takes the Greek animal name as hippopotamus.
items.cn: 拉丁语把希腊语动物名收作 hippopotamus。

items.en: Hippopotamus appears in English writing, probably through Latin or Old French.
items.cn: hippopotamus 在十四世纪的英语文献中出现，可能经由拉丁语或古法语传入。

items.en: Shortened forms such as hippo spread in speech and in books for children.
items.cn: hippo 这样的缩短形式在口语与儿童读物中流行开来。

items.en: Hippo is the ordinary word for the animal in most everyday English.
items.cn: 在现代英语的大多数日常场合，hippo 已经是这种动物的通行叫法。

note.en: Hippo is the clipped river horse of Greek origin, next to its full form and to other big river animals.
note.cn: hippo 是源自希腊语「河中之马」的截短词，与它的完整形式以及其他大型河栖动物相邻。

entries.definition: the formal name of the animal
entries.definitionCN: 这种动物的完整正式名称

entries.definition: a Latin-style plural of the full name
entries.definitionCN: 完整名称的拉丁式复数，多见于科普文章

entries.definition: an ancient course for horse racing
entries.definitionCN: 古代的赛马场（与 hippo 共享希腊语 hippos「马」）

entries.definition: the short name for a large horned African animal
entries.definitionCN: 犀牛（同样是由长名截短的常见简称）

entries.definition: a large river reptile with a long snout
entries.definitionCN: 鳄鱼；另一种常见于河流的大型爬行动物

entries.definition: a huge grey animal with a trunk
entries.definitionCN: 大象；与河马同属非洲的大型灰皮动物

normalIntro.en: Hippo is the front half of the Greek river horse, the half people say when the full word is too long.
normalIntro.cn: hippo 是希腊语「河中之马」的前半段，也是全称太长时人们愿意说的那一半。

normal.en: Greek hippos means horse, so hippo begins as the horse half of the long name.
normal.cn: 希腊语 hippos 表示「马」，所以 hippo 一开始就是那个长名字中「马」这一半。

normal.en: Hippos is the regular plural, used as in a group of hippos.
normal.cn: hippos 是规则复数，比如 a group of hippos 一群河马。

normal.en: The full form hippopotamus stays for museums, zoos, and formal writing.
normal.cn: 完整形式 hippopotamus 留在博物馆、动物园与正式写作中。

normal.en: Rhino and hippo are both clipped animal names made from their long forms.
normal.cn: rhino 和 hippo 都是从长名截短的动物简称，路子完全一样。

normal.en: Hippodrome keeps the same horse element for a racing track.
normal.cn: hippodrome（赛马场）保留了同一个表示「马」的成分。

abstract.en: Picture a grey hill rising slowly out of the water, eyes just above the surface.
abstract.cn: 想象一座灰色小山慢慢从水里升起，眼睛恰好露出水面。

abstract.en: Picture a toddler pointing at a sign that says hippo in big letters.
abstract.cn: 想象一个幼儿指着写着 hippo 大字招牌的画面。

abstract.en: Picture a painted wall in an old tomb with a blue hippo beside a pool.
abstract.cn: 想象一面古墓壁画，池子旁边画着一头蓝色的河马。

examples.en: Hippos spend the hottest hours of the day in the water.
examples.cn: 河马会把一天里最热的几个小时都泡在水里。

examples.en: We watched a hippo open its enormous mouth at the zoo.
examples.cn: 我们在动物园看一头河马张开大嘴。

examples.en: The sign near the river says that hippos live here.
examples.cn: 河边的那块牌子上写着这里住着河马。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「黑泡」——一头「黑」褐色的大兽整天「泡」在水里，一个词就记住了；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 hippos（马）+ potamos（河流）→ hippopotamos（河中之马）→ 拉丁语 hippopotamus → 十四世纪英语 hippopotamus → 十九世纪起口语截短为 hippo，核心义「泡在河里的大型兽」。

sensesIntro.en: Hippo starts as the everyday name for the animal, then works as a nickname for heavy things, and also carries the mythic weight of the ancient Nile hippo.
sensesIntro.cn: hippo 先是这种动物的日常叫法，再被用作笨重之物的绰号，同时承载着古尼罗河地区赋予河马的神话意味。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a huge grey animal half sunk in a river.
core.cn: 核心意象：一头巨大的灰色动物半沉在河里。

branches.en: The real animal is the core sense of hippo.
branches.cn: 真实的动物是 hippo 的核心义项。

branches.en: A nickname for heavy things is the informal sense.
branches.cn: 给笨重之物起绰号是非正式义项。

branches.en: The mythic hippo is the religious and artistic sense.
branches.cn: 神话中的河马是宗教与艺术义项。

branches.en: Both the animal and the goddess share one body in ancient art.
branches.cn: 在古代艺术中，动物与女神共用同一副身躯。

branches.en: The animal and the nickname share the same weight and slowness.
branches.cn: 动物本身与绰号共享同样的沉重与迟缓。

intro.en: Hippo is a Greek animal name cut in half, with hippopotamus, hippos, and the horse element kept in several other English words.
intro.cn: hippo 是一个被截成一半的希腊语动物名，周围有 hippopotamus、复数 hippos，以及保留「马」这一成分的若干英语词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin form hippopotamus keeps the Greek pieces hippos for horse and potamos for river.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 hippopotamus 保留了希腊语的两个部分：hippo 表示马，potamus 表示河流。

items.example: The combining form hippo- is the horse part.
items.exampleCN: 构词成分 hippo- 就是表示「马」的部分。

items.example: Hippos is the Greek word for horse.
items.exampleCN: hippos 是希腊语中的「马」。

items.example: Potamos supplies the river of the long name.
items.exampleCN: potamos 为那个长名字提供「河」的含义。

items.example: The element -potamus still ends the full name.
items.exampleCN: 构词成分 -potamus 至今仍在全称的末尾。

items.example: Hippopotamus is the full form of the name.
items.exampleCN: hippopotamus 是名称的完整形式。

items.meaning: the short name for the animal
items.example: Hippo keeps only the horse half.
items.exampleCN: hippo 只保留了「马」那一半。

items.example: Hippos is the plural for the short name.
items.exampleCN: hippos 是简称的复数形式。

items.example: The suffix -drome builds hippodrome and aerodrome.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -drome 构成 hippodrome 与 aerodrome。

items.example: Hippodrome is literally a horse course.
items.exampleCN: hippodrome 字面意思就是「马之道」。

items.example: Mesopotamian carries the river element in a place name.
items.exampleCN: Mesopotamian 在地名里带着同一个「河流」成分。

definition_zh: 发嘶嘶声；发嘘声；嘶嘶声；嘘声；漏气声
definition_en: to make a long sound like a stream of air escaping, and to show dislike of a speaker with that sound
core_image: 水珠落在烧热的铁板上，腾起一道又长又尖的嘶嘶声
scene: 厨房里，一只湿手不小心碰到了烧热的铁锅。A tiny drop of water hit the hot pan and hissed for a second.
sceneCN: 这里 hiss 是「发出嘶嘶声」（第 1 个义项：像气流漏出或水汽腾起时那种长长的高频声）；句意：一小滴水落在热锅上，嘶嘶响了一秒。

pos.zh: 发嘶嘶声；（电器或机器）发出沙沙的电流声
对……发出嘘声；用嘘声表示（不满）

derivatives.zh: hiss 加 -ing 构成，义为「嘶嘶声；嘶嘶响的」，如 the hissing of a kettle
hissing 加 -ly 构成，义为「嘶嘶地」，描述声音持续发出的样子
hiss 加过去分词词尾 -ed 转作形容词，多见于戏剧说明，义为「带着嘘声的；嘶嘶吐出的」

senses.title: To make a long airy sound
senses.definition: to make or give out a long high sound like escaping air, steam, or a hot surface cooling
senses.definitionCN: 发出一种又长又高的声音，像漏气、蒸汽喷出或炽热表面冷却时的声响
senses.example: The kettle began to hiss as the water boiled.
senses.exampleCN: 水烧开时，水壶开始嘶嘶作响。
senses.why: The word was shaped by the sound itself, so the core sense is simply to produce that rushing airy noise.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本身就是照着声音造的，所以核心义项就是「发出那种带气流的长音」，这是声音自身塑形出来的结果。

senses.title: To show dislike with a hiss
senses.definition: to make a long sharp sound as an act of disapproval or mockery at a speaker, player, or performer
senses.definitionCN: 对发言者、球员或表演者发出又长又尖的声音，表示不赞同或嘲弄
senses.example: The crowd hissed when the referee gave a penalty.
senses.exampleCN: 裁判判罚点球时，观众发出嘘声。
senses.why: Audiences have long turned the escaping air sound into a tool of public disapproval, so the sound became the act.
senses.whyCN: 观众早就把这种「漏气」般的声音变成公开表态的工具，于是声音本身就成了评价或抗议的动作。

senses.title: The sound itself
senses.definition: a long high sound of escaping air or steam, or a burst of such sounds from a crowd
senses.definitionCN: 漏气或蒸汽发出的长而高的声音，或人群一齐发出的这种声音
senses.example: We heard a faint hiss from the leaking tyre.
senses.exampleCN: 我们听见漏气的轮胎发出轻微的嘶嘶声。
senses.why: Every verb of pure sound also works as a noun, and hiss follows that pattern without changing its shape.
senses.whyCN: 每一个纯粹描摹声音的动词都同时是名词，hiss 也循着这条老路，词形一点不变就当名词用。

senses.title: An angry animal sound
senses.definition: the warning sound a snake, cat, or goose makes with air pushed through a narrow gap
senses.definitionCN: 蛇、猫或鹅受惊警告时，把气流从窄缝里挤出来发出的声音
senses.example: The cat backed away and hissed at the dog.
senses.exampleCN: 那只猫后退几步，冲狗嘶嘶地叫。
senses.why: Animal threats run on exactly the same airy sound, so hiss spread to snakes and geese as a warning call.
senses.whyCN: 动物的威吓用的正是同样的气流声，于是 hiss 自然扩展到了蛇与鹅身上的警告声。

senses.title: A spoken whisper
senses.titleCN: 低声急促地说；气声说出
senses.definition: to say something in a sharp, low, breathy voice, usually because it is meant to be heard by one person only
senses.definitionCN: 用尖细、低沉、带气声的嗓音说话，通常只让一个人听见
senses.example: She hissed a warning across the quiet room.
senses.exampleCN: 她在安静的房间里压低声音发出一声警告。
senses.why: A real whisper also lets air hiss between the teeth, so the speaking verb borrows the sound for urgent quiet speech.
senses.whyCN: 真正的低语同样让气从齿缝里嘶嘶泄出，于是这个动词被借来表示「压低嗓门、急切耳语」的说法。

intro.en: Hiss is an imitative word: English shaped it from the sound itself, though a similar hissen appears in the Germanic languages.
intro.cn: hiss 是拟声词：英语直接照着声音造出它，日耳曼诸语言中也有相近的 hissen 形式。

items.en: A hissing form such as hissen appears in Middle Low German, and the sound word is widespread in the Germanic family.
items.cn: 中古低地德语中有 hissen 一类表示「嘶嘶作响」的词，这个拟声词在日耳曼语族里相当普遍。

items.en: The verb hissen appears in the Middle English period for the sound of escaping air.
items.cn: 中古英语时期出现动词 hissen，指漏气之声。

items.en: Hiss is used for the sound of snakes and steam, and for the crowd noise of disapproval.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，hiss 既指蛇与蒸汽的声音，也指人群表示不满时发出的嘘声。

items.en: The noun hiss settles into the same shape as the verb, and writers use it for mechanical sounds.
items.cn: 十九世纪，名词 hiss 定型成与动词完全相同的拼写，作家也用它与机器噪声搭配。

items.en: Hiss keeps the same spellings and meanings, from kettles and tyres to angry crowds and radio static.
items.cn: 现代英语中 hiss 的拼写与含义基本未变，从水壶、轮胎一直到愤怒的人群与收音机噪点。

note.en: Hiss belongs to the family of sound words, standing beside its noun form and the other words for airy or sibilant noise.
note.cn: hiss 属于拟声词一族，和它的名词形式以及其他表示气流声、齿擦音的词相邻。

entries.definition: the act or sound of making a hiss
entries.definitionCN: 发出嘶嘶声这个动作或这种声音

entries.definition: made a hiss in the past
entries.definitionCN: 过去发出过嘶嘶声（动词过去式）

entries.definition: to make someone quiet
entries.definitionCN: 让某人安静下来；只是音节相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to make a clear high sound by pushing air through the lips or a small opening
entries.definitionCN: 吹口哨；通过嘴唇或小孔挤出气流发出清晰的高音

entries.definition: to make the cracking sound of frying food
entries.definitionCN: 煎炸食物时滋滋响

entries.definition: to shout a low sound to show dislike
entries.definitionCN: 叫倒好；用低沉的一声表示不满

normalIntro.en: Hiss is a sound you can almost hear in the letters: air pushed through a small gap.
normalIntro.cn: hiss 是一个几乎能从字母里听出来的词：气流被从小缝里挤出去。

normal.en: Hiss doubles its final s after -ss-, so the third person form is hisses.
normal.cn: hiss 本身以 -ss 结尾，所以三单形式是 hisses。

normal.en: The past tense is not hised but hissed, with the final s doubled before -ed.
normal.cn: 过去式不是 hised，而是 hissed：末尾的 s 先双写，再加 -ed。

normal.en: Use hiss at for the audience and hiss of for the sound of steam.
normal.cn: 对观众发嘘声用 hiss at，描述蒸汽的声音用 hiss of。

normal.en: The noun hiss has the same spelling as the verb, so the shape never changes.
normal.cn: 名词 hiss 与动词拼写完全相同，词形从不变化。

normal.en: Compare boo: boo is a short burst of dislike, hiss is the long airy version of the same feeling.
normal.cn: 对比 boo：boo 是短促的一声倒好，hiss 是同样情绪被拉长后的气流声版本。

abstract.en: Picture a splash of water hitting a hot iron plate and turning into steam.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴水落在烧红的铁板上，一下化成蒸汽。

abstract.en: Picture a whole lecture hall breathing out one long angry sound at a bad joke.
abstract.cn: 想象整个讲堂对一句烂笑话一起吐出一声长长的抗议。

abstract.en: Picture the thin line of a kettle whistle in a quiet kitchen.
abstract.cn: 想象安静的厨房里，水壶哨音拉出一声细细的嘶嘶声。

examples.en: The steam hissed as it escaped from the valve.
examples.cn: 蒸汽从阀门里冲出来时嘶嘶作响。

examples.en: The snake raised its head and hissed softly.
examples.cn: 那条蛇抬起头，轻轻地发出嘶嘶声。

examples.en: When the speech ended, a hiss came from the back of the hall.
examples.cn: 演讲结束时，大厅后方传来一声嘘声。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「嘶」——模仿蛇吐信时的那一声，读到 hiss 脑子里就自动配音；这只是读音联想，虽然拟声确是造词方式，但不据此推断词源细节。

root: 拟声词（声音先于写法）：日耳曼语族中 hissen 一类表示「嘶嘶作响」的形式 → 中古英语 hissen → 英语 hiss，核心义「气从窄缝挤出的长音」。

sensesIntro.en: Hiss starts from one airy sound, then becomes the act of public disapproval, the identical-looking noun, an animal warning, and a breathy way of speaking.
sensesIntro.cn: hiss 从一个气流声起家，随后变成公开表达不满的动作、拼写不变的名词、动物的警告声，最后成为带气声的说话方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a jet of steam or water escaping a narrow gap.
core.cn: 核心意象：一股蒸汽或水流从窄缝里冲出来。

branches.en: The escaping air sound is the core sense.
branches.cn: 气流泄漏声是核心义项。

branches.en: The crowd using that sound to swell a complaint is the public sense.
branches.cn: 人群把这个声音用来表达抗议，是公共义项。

branches.en: The very same sound, named as a thing, is the noun sense.
branches.cn: 把同一个声音当作事物来命名，就是名词义项。

branches.en: The animal warning is the oldest use of the sound.
branches.cn: 动物的警告声是这种声音最古老的用法。

branches.en: Speaking through the teeth reuses the airy sound for a quiet but urgent voice.
branches.cn: 从齿缝里说话，借用了同一种气流声来表达压抑而急切的嗓音。

intro.en: Hiss is a bare imitative stem with almost no affixes, built up through -s, -ed, -ing, and -ly endings in its family.
intro.cn: hiss 几乎不带词缀，是一个纯粹的拟声词干，词族主要靠 -s、-ed、-ing、-ly 这些词尾长出来。

latinIntro.en: Hiss has no Latin source, though Latin has its own pure sound verb sibilare, which was borrowed into English as sibilant.
latinIntro.cn: hiss 没有拉丁来源；不过拉丁语本身也有纯拟声动词 sibilare，后来以 sibilant 的形式被借进英语。

items.example: Hiss is shaped directly from the sound.
items.exampleCN: hiss 是直接照着声音造出来的。

items.meaningCN: 表示长擦音的词尾拼写
items.example: The -ss ending keeps the airy noise of the word.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ss 保留了这个词的气流声感。

items.example: The ending -s gives the third person hisses.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -s 构成了三单形式 hisses。

items.example: Hisses is the third person form of the verb.
items.exampleCN: hisses 是动词的三单形式。

items.example: The ending -ed gives the past form hissed.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成过去式 hissed。

items.example: Hissed also works as an adjective in drama notes.
items.exampleCN: hissed 在戏剧说明里也可作形容词。

items.example: The ending -ing gives the noun hissing.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成名词 hissing。

items.example: Hissing names a sound that goes on and on.
items.exampleCN: hissing 表示一种持续不断的声音。

items.example: The suffix -ly builds the adverb hissingly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成副词 hissingly。

items.example: Sibilant is the Latin way of naming a hissing sound.
items.exampleCN: sibilant 是描述嘶音的拉丁式说法。

definition_zh: 迄今为止；到目前为止；在这一时期以前
definition_en: up to this time; until now or until the point being discussed
core_image: 从远处伸来的一只手，在一道时间线上一直划到现在这个点
scene: 一份评估报告在开头回顾过去几年的情况，结尾要交代到此刻为止的整体判断。The committee noted that the scheme had hitherto failed to attract any foreign investors.
sceneCN: 这里 hitherto 是「迄今为止」（第 1 个义项：从过去一直延续到现在）；句意：委员会指出，该计划迄今未能吸引任何外国投资者。

pos.zh: 迄今为止；到目前为止；在这一时期以前

derivatives.zh: 到这里；向此处（古旧或书面用语），是 hitherto 的前半部分
到那里；向那边，与 hither 同源的方位副词伙伴
向这里；朝这个方向，由 hither 加表方向的词尾构成

senses.title: Up to this time
senses.definition: until now; up to the present moment or the time being discussed
senses.definitionCN: 到现在为止；到此刻或所讨论的时间点为止
senses.example: The results have hitherto been rather disappointing.
senses.exampleCN: 到目前为止，结果一直颇令人失望。
senses.why: The word is built from hither, meaning to this place, plus to, so its first job is marking a line that runs all the way up to here and now.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 hither（到这里）加 to 构成，所以第一层意思就是把一条线一路拉到此时此地。

senses.title: Before a change or turning point
senses.definition: before a particular event or stage that changes the situation afterwards
senses.definitionCN: 在某个事件或阶段之前，此后情况发生了变化
senses.example: Hitherto, the clinic had only treated adults.
senses.exampleCN: 在此之前，这家诊所只接诊成年人。
senses.why: Because the line stops at the point of speaking, it naturally contrasts what came before with what happens next.
senses.whyCN: 因为这条线止于说话的这一刻，它自然把「之前」与「之后」对照起来，成为转折的分界。

senses.title: Previously in the written record
senses.definition: in earlier studies, reports or written works, before the present one
senses.definitionCN: 在此前的研究、报告或著作中，相对于当前这一份而言
senses.example: Hitherto undiscovered letters were found in the archive.
senses.exampleCN: 档案馆里发现了此前未被发现的信件。
senses.why: In academic writing the line is drawn at the paper or study in hand, so hitherto means in all the earlier record.
senses.whyCN: 在学术写作里，这条线划在眼前这篇论文或研究这里，所以 hitherto 指此前全部记载。

intro.en: Hitherto joins Middle English hither, meaning to this place, with the preposition to used in the older sense of up to.
intro.cn: hitherto 由中古英语 hither（到这里）与介词 to（旧义「直到」）合成。

items.en: The adverb hider means to this place, in contrast with þider, to that place.
items.cn: 古英语副词 hider 意为「到这里」，与表示「到那里」的 þider 相对。

items.en: The preposition to covers direction and also limit, as in up to that point.
items.cn: 介词 to 既表示方向，也表示界限，如「直到那一点」。

items.en: Hither and to are first joined in one adverb, spelled in several ways, meaning up to now.
items.cn: 中古英语中 hither 与 to 首次合为一个副词，拼法不统一，意为「直到现在」。

items.en: The settled spelling hitherto appears, and the word becomes common in legal and scholarly prose.
items.cn: 固定拼写 hitherto 出现，并在法律与学术文章中广泛使用。

items.en: Hitherto is now formal and often bookish, while so far and until now dominate speech.
items.cn: 现代 hitherto 正式而偏书面，口语中多用 so far 与 until now。

note.en: Hitherto sits in an old family of here, there and where adverbs, and it competes with plainer time words such as so far.
note.cn: hitherto 属于 here、there、where 式的古方位副词家族，并与更朴素的 so far 一类时间词竞争。

entries.definition: to this place; here
entries.definitionCN: 到这里；向此处，是构词的前半部分

entries.definition: to that place
entries.definitionCN: 到那里；向那边，与 hither 成对

entries.definition: to what place
entries.definitionCN: 往何处，同属古方位副词

entries.definition: in various directions
entries.definitionCN: 这里那里地；四处，由 hither 组成的习语

entries.definition: until now
entries.definitionCN: 到目前为止，口语中最常用的对应说法

entries.definition: up to the present time
entries.definitionCN: 直到现在

entries.definition: at an earlier time
entries.definitionCN: 先前；以前，侧重「过去某一时刻」，不含延续到现在

entries.definition: as at the present moment
entries.definitionCN: 迄今为止，与 hitherto 语气接近

normalIntro.en: Hitherto is a clock hand that keeps sweeping up to this very second before it stops.
normalIntro.cn: hitherto 就是一根不停扫动的钟表针，一直扫到这一秒才停下。

normal.en: Split it as hither plus to, meaning up to here.
normal.cn: 把它拆成 hither 加 to，就是「一直到此处」。

normal.en: Hither means to this place, so a line from there to here ends in the present.
normal.cn: hither 意为「到这里」，所以一条从过去画到这里的线，终点就在现在。

normal.en: Pair it with thither: hither is here, thither is there.
normal.cn: 与 thither 配对：hither 是「这里」，thither 是「那里」。

normal.en: Hitherto usually comes before the verb, as in had hitherto failed.
normal.cn: hitherto 通常放在动词之前，如 had hitherto failed 这一搭配。

normal.en: For everyday speech use so far; keep hitherto for formal writing.
normal.cn: 口语用 so far，正式书面才用 hitherto。

abstract.en: Picture a film reel unspooling until the current frame.
abstract.cn: 想象一卷胶片一直放映到此刻这一帧。

abstract.en: Imagine a bridge built from the far past that stops right under your feet.
abstract.cn: 想象一座从遥远过去修来的桥，桥头恰好停在你脚下。

abstract.en: Think of a footnote that says everything up to this page.
abstract.cn: 想象一条脚注写着：本页之前的全部内容。

examples.en: The disease, hitherto confined to the south, has now spread nationwide.
examples.cn: 这种疾病此前仅限于南方，现在已经蔓延到全国。

examples.en: She was hitherto unknown to the public but is now a household name.
examples.cn: 她此前不为人知，如今却已家喻户晓。

examples.en: The plan had hitherto been judged too expensive to carry out.
examples.cn: 这个计划此前一直被认为耗资过大而无法实施。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「嘿，着吐」——嘿，一直撑到吐，也就是熬到了现在；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 hider（到这里）＋ to（直到）→ 中古英语 hither to（直到此处）→ 现代 hitherto，核心义「从过去一直到此刻」。

sensesIntro.en: Hitherto first means up to now, then marks the point just before a change, and finally refers to the earlier written record in academic work.
sensesIntro.cn: hitherto 先指直到现在，再指出某个转折之前，最后指学术文本中此前的记载。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line drawn from the distant past that stops at this moment.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条从遥远过去画来、止于此刻的线。

branches.en: Up to now is the everyday meaning of the line ending at the present.
branches.cn: 直到现在是这条线止于此刻的日常用法。

branches.en: Before a turning point is the same line stopping just before an event.
branches.cn: 转折之前是同一条线停在事件发生的那一刻。

branches.en: The earlier record sense lives mostly in research and scholarly prose.
branches.cn: 此前记载这一义项多见于研究与学术文章。

branches.en: Up to now and before a change often appear together when a report compares past and present.
branches.cn: 报告比较今昔时，直到现在与转折之前常常同时出现。

branches.en: Earlier studies set the stage for the turning points that new papers describe.
branches.cn: 此前研究为新论文所描述的转折铺好了背景。

intro.en: Hitherto is a compound adverb built from the old directional word hither and the preposition to, and it anchors a small family of hither, thither and whither.
intro.cn: hitherto 是由古方位词 hither 与介词 to 构成的合成副词，并与 hither、thither、whither 同属一个小家族。

latinIntro.en: Latin has huc, meaning to this place, a close cousin of hither, though the English form itself is native Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 huc 意为「到这里」，与 hither 意思接近，但英语 hither 本身是日耳曼语固有词。

items.example: Hither still survives in the literary idiom come hither.
items.exampleCN: hither 仍保存在书面习语 come hither 中。

items.example: Thither is the matching adverb for that place.
items.exampleCN: thither 是表示「那里」的配对方位副词。

items.example: Whither completes the here there what set.
items.exampleCN: whither 补全了「这里、那里、何处」这一组。

items.example: The suffix -ward builds hitherward from hither.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ward 由 hither 构成 hitherward。

items.example: Hitherto joins hither with the preposition to.
items.exampleCN: hitherto 把 hither 与介词 to 连在一起。

items.example: Here to means up to a limit, not direction.
items.exampleCN: 这里 to 指「直到某一界限」，而不是方向。

items.example: Thereto uses the same to with there.
items.exampleCN: thereto 用同样的 to 与 there 组合。

items.example: Heretofore is the formal partner of hitherto.
items.exampleCN: heretofore 是 hitherto 的正式近亲。

items.example: So far is the plain spoken replacement for hitherto.
items.exampleCN: so far 是 hitherto 的口语替代说法。

latinEntries.meaning: up to this point, so far

definition_zh: 嘶哑的；沙哑的；声音粗哑的
definition_en: sounding rough and harsh, usually because of a sore throat or too much shouting
core_image: 喊了整场球赛之后，喉咙里像塞满了砂纸，一开口就是沙沙的气声
scene: 球迷在看台上喊了整晚，第二天开会时一开口就只剩下气声。After cheering all night at the stadium, he was so hoarse that he could not speak properly.
sceneCN: 这里 hoarse 是「嘶哑的」（第 1 个义项：嗓子因喊叫或生病而沙哑）；句意：在球场喊了一整晚之后，他嗓子哑得说不出话来。

pos.zh: 嘶哑的；沙哑的；声音粗哑的

derivatives.zh: 沙哑地，由形容词加词尾 -ly 构成
嘶哑；沙哑，由形容词加名词词尾 -ness 构成
使沙哑；变得沙哑，由形容词加动词词尾 -en 构成

senses.title: A rough and rasping voice
senses.definition: having a rough, harsh voice, often from a cold, shouting or overuse
senses.definitionCN: 嗓音粗糙刺耳，常因感冒、喊叫或过度用嗓引起
senses.example: His voice was hoarse after the marathon.
senses.exampleCN: 马拉松跑完之后，他的声音哑了。
senses.why: The word originally means harsh or rough on the throat, so it starts with the physical rasp of a tired voice.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初形容喉咙发涩粗糙，所以第一层意思就是疲倦嗓音里那种沙沙的摩擦感。

senses.title: A harsh sound beyond the voice
senses.definition: describing any sound that is harsh, rough and grating, such as a cough or an instrument
senses.definitionCN: 形容咳嗽、乐器等任何粗哑刺耳的声音
senses.example: A hoarse cough came from the next room.
senses.exampleCN: 隔壁房间传来一声粗哑的咳嗽。
senses.why: Once the rough quality is separated from the throat, the word can describe any sound that grates in the same way.
senses.whyCN: 当这种粗糙质感从喉咙中脱离出来，就能用来形容任何同样刺耳的声音。

senses.title: A strained, angry tone
senses.definition: a way of speaking that sounds strained, angry or charged with strong feeling
senses.definitionCN: 听起来紧绷、愤怒或饱含强烈情绪的语气
senses.example: She replied in a hoarse whisper that made him step back.
senses.exampleCN: 她用沙哑的低语回答，吓得他后退了一步。
senses.why: When feeling presses on the voice, the throat tightens, so a hoarse tone becomes a signal of barely held emotion.
senses.whyCN: 情绪压迫嗓音时喉咙会发紧，于是沙哑的语调就成了竭力克制的情绪信号。

intro.en: Hoarse is a native Germanic word, related to Old Norse har, meaning grey, and to the modern scan of rough, husky sound.
intro.cn: hoarse 是日耳曼语固有词，与古诺斯语 har（灰色、灰白）相关，词义从「粗糙」转向「嗓音沙哑」。

items.en: A root meaning hoary or rough is reconstructable as the source, but the form is uncertain and marked as reconstructed.
items.cn: 一般认为可重构出一个意为「灰白、粗糙」的词根，但具体形式不确定，属重构推测。

items.en: Old Norse har means grey or hoary and also lumpy or rough.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 har 意为灰色、灰白，也可指表面粗糙不平。

items.en: An early English form describes a voice that is rough and thick.
items.cn: 古英语晚期已有一个形式用来形容嗓音粗涩厚重。

items.en: Hoos and hoors spellings settle into hoarse, used of voices and throats.
items.cn: 中古英语中 hoos、hoors 等拼法逐渐统一为 hoarse，用于嗓音和喉咙。

items.en: The word widens from the throat to coughs, whispers and any grating sound.
items.cn: 现代英语中词义从喉咙扩展到咳嗽、低语以及任何刺耳的声音。

note.en: Hoarse shares its rough sound with the spelling twin horse and moves in the same field as husky, raspy and croaky.
note.cn: hoarse 的沙哑质感与拼写相近的 horse 容易混淆，并与 husky、raspy、croaky 同属嗓音义场。

entries.definition: a large animal ridden by people
entries.definitionCN: 马；读音与 hoarse 相同，但只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a rough, rasping voice
entries.definitionCN: 沙哑的嗓音，最常见的搭配之一

entries.definition: the state of being hoarse
entries.definitionCN: 嘶哑，由 hoarse 加 -ness 构成

entries.definition: in a hoarse way
entries.definitionCN: 沙哑地，由 hoarse 加 -ly 构成

entries.definition: low and slightly rough, often in an attractive way
entries.definitionCN: 低沉微哑的，常带磁性或吸引力

entries.definition: harsh and grating, like a file on wood
entries.definitionCN: 刺耳的；粗砂般的

entries.definition: sounding like a frog, weak and unsteady
entries.definitionCN: 像青蛙叫一样低沉不稳的

entries.definition: low and rough, often suggesting a blunt manner
entries.definitionCN: 粗声粗气的，常暗示态度生硬

normalIntro.en: Hoarse is the sound of a throat worn thin, rough as unpolished wood.
normalIntro.cn: hoarse 就是喉咙被磨薄后的声音，粗糙得像没打磨的木头。

normal.en: Listen for the same vowel as horse, but keep the h and r more breathy.
normal.cn: 注意它的元音与 horse 相同，但 h 和 r 更要带气声。

normal.en: A hoarse voice is a rough voice, so pair the word with voice or throat.
normal.cn: hoarse voice 就是粗哑的嗓音，所以常与 voice 或 throat 连用。

normal.en: To shout oneself hoarse is a favourite collocation: keep shouting until the voice gives out.
normal.cn: shout oneself hoarse 是高频搭配：喊到嗓子哑掉。

normal.en: The endings -ly and -ness build hoarsely and hoarseness.
normal.cn: 加 -ly 与 -ness 可构成 hoarsely 与 hoarseness。

normal.en: Compare husky, which is pleasantly rough, with hoarse, which usually signals illness or strain.
normal.cn: 对比 husky：husky 是迷人的低哑，hoarse 多表示生病或用力过度。

abstract.en: Picture a singer at the end of a long concert sipping warm water.
abstract.cn: 想象一位歌手在长演唱会结束后小口喝着温水。

abstract.en: Think of a door hinge that has not been oiled for years.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇多年没有上油的合页门，吱呀作响。

abstract.en: Imagine a whisper forced through sandpaper instead of air.
abstract.cn: 想象一句低语被迫穿过砂纸，而不是穿过空气。

examples.en: The teacher sounded hoarse because she had been lecturing all morning.
examples.cn: 老师上午一直在讲课，声音听起来沙哑了。

examples.en: He shouted himself hoarse trying to be heard over the crowd.
examples.cn: 为了压过人群的声音，他喊哑了嗓子。

examples.en: Her hoarse reply hinted that she had been crying.
examples.cn: 她沙哑的回答暗示她刚刚哭过。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「嚎嘶」——扯着嗓子嚎，声音又嘶又哑，正是 hoarse；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 日耳曼语词根（一般认为与「灰白、粗糙」相关，具体形式为重构推测）→ 古诺斯语 har（灰色的；粗糙的）→ 古英语 hās（嗓音粗涩）→ 现代英语 hoarse，核心义「粗糙刺耳的声音」。

sensesIntro.en: Hoarse starts from a rough, rasping voice, widens to any harsh sound, and finally colours a tone with anger or strained feeling.
sensesIntro.cn: hoarse 先指粗哑的嗓音，再扩展到各种刺耳的声音，最后用来形容愤怒或紧绷的语气。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a throat rubbed raw, breathing out sandpaper instead of sound.
core.cn: 核心意象：被磨得发涩的喉咙，吐出的不是声音而是砂纸般的摩擦。

branches.en: The rasping voice is the first and most common sense.
branches.cn: 粗哑的嗓音是最主要、最常见的义项。

branches.en: Any harsh sound is the voice sense extended to coughs and instruments.
branches.cn: 任何刺耳的声音，是嗓音义扩展到咳嗽与乐器。

branches.en: A strained tone is the emotional reading of the same rough quality.
branches.cn: 紧绷的语气是同一种粗糙质感的情绪化解读。

branches.en: A hoarse voice and a hoarse cough both come from an irritated throat.
branches.cn: 沙哑的嗓音与粗哑的咳嗽都源自受刺激的喉咙。

branches.en: A hoarse whisper carries both physical roughness and held-back feeling.
branches.cn: 沙哑的低语同时带有生理上的粗糙与压抑的情绪。

intro.en: Hoarse is a native base word with no productive prefix, but its endings -ly, -ness and -en spin off a tidy adjective family.
intro.cn: hoarse 是日耳曼语固有词，本身没有能产前缀，但词尾 -ly、-ness、-en 构成了一个小而整齐的形容词家族。

latinIntro.en: Classical Latin has no direct cognate, but Latin raucus, meaning hoarse, explains the English word raucous.
latinIntro.cn: 古典拉丁语没有直接同源词，但拉丁语 raucus（沙哑的）对应英语 raucous。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms hoarsely from hoarse.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 由 hoarse 构成 hoarsely。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms hoarseness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 hoarseness。

items.example: The rare verb hoarsen uses the suffix -en.
items.exampleCN: 少用动词 hoarsen 用到词尾 -en。

items.example: Hoarse keeps its Old English rough sound sense.
items.exampleCN: hoarse 保留着古英语里「粗糙声音」的意思。

items.meaning: produced with vibration of the vocal cords
items.example: A voiced consonant is not hoarse in the medical sense.
items.exampleCN: 浊辅音并不属于医学意义上的沙哑。

items.meaning: to scrape with a rough sound
items.example: Rasp explains the raspy neighbour of hoarse.
items.exampleCN: rasp 解释了 hoarse 的近义词 raspy。

items.meaning: to write or say the letters of a word
items.example: Do not spell hoarse with two o letters.
items.exampleCN: 拼写 hoarse 时不要写成两个 o。

items.example: Horse shares the sound but not the spelling of hoarse.
items.exampleCN: horse 与 hoarse 发音相同但拼写不同。

items.example: Harsh gives the general quality behind hoarse.
items.exampleCN: harsh 概括了 hoarse 背后的粗糙质感。

definition_zh: 曲棍球；冰球；冰球运动
definition_en: a team game in which players use curved sticks to hit a ball or a puck into a goal
core_image: 两名球员弯腰挥动弯头球棒，把球赶向球场两端的球门
scene: 冬天湖面结冰，孩子们拿根棍子就在冰上追赶一个小圆盘。Every winter our school ice hockey team trains on the frozen lake.
sceneCN: 这里 hockey 是「冰球」（第 2 个义项：在冰面或硬地板上进行的冰球运动）；句意：每年冬天我们学校的冰球队都在结冰的湖面上训练。

forms.label: 复数（口语，指多场球赛或球具）
动词过去式（口语转用，罕见）

derivatives.zh: 曲棍球或冰球运动员，由 hockey 加表示人的词尾 -ist 构成
类似曲棍球的，由 hockey 加 -like 构成

senses.title: The game played with curved sticks
senses.definition: a team sport in which players use hooked sticks to drive a ball into the opponents goal
senses.definitionCN: 一种团队运动，球员用弯头球棒把球推进对方球门
senses.example: Hockey is the national sport of India and Pakistan.
senses.exampleCN: 曲棍球是印度和巴基斯坦的国民运动。
senses.why: The game takes its name from the crooked curved stick of the old French word hoquet, so the name is built on the tool itself.
senses.whyCN: 这项运动的名字来自古法语 hoquet 所指的弯头棍，所以词义从一开始就长在「球棒」上。

senses.title: Ice hockey on the rink
senses.definition: the version played on ice, by players on skates, using a flat puck instead of a ball
senses.definitionCN: 在冰面进行、穿冰鞋、用扁平的冰球而非球来打的版本
senses.example: Ice hockey is one of the fastest team sports in the world.
senses.exampleCN: 冰球是世界上节奏最快的团队运动之一。
senses.why: British usage kept hockey for the winter ice game, so the same stick-and-goal image moved onto a frozen surface.
senses.whyCN: 英国用法把 hockey 留给冬季冰上比赛，于是同一套「球棒与球门」的意象搬到了冰面上。

senses.title: The gear rather than the game
senses.definition: informal use for the hockey stick, puck or other equipment of the game
senses.definitionCN: 口语中泛指球棒、冰球或其他比赛装备
senses.example: She grabbed her hockey and ran to the field.
senses.exampleCN: 她抓起球杆冲向了场地。
senses.why: Because the word grew from the shape of the stick, informal speech easily shifts it back onto the piece of equipment.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个词本来就长在球棒的形状上，口语里很容易又滑回指那件装备本身。

intro.en: The origin of hockey is uncertain; the most favoured explanation links it to a kind of hooked stick, while other writers also propose an Old Irish word for a ball.
intro.cn: hockey 的词源尚无定论；最流行的解释与一种弯头球棒相关，也有学者提出来自古爱尔兰语中表示「球」的词。

items.en: The diminutive hoquet or hoket can name a curved shepherd stick, from hoc, a hook, a form whose derivation is itself debated.
items.cn: 古法语指小词 hoquet 或 hoket 可指牧羊人的弯头棍，来源词 hoc（钩子）本身也存疑。

items.en: The earliest known record of hockey in English dates to about 1527, when a Galway law bans the ball and stick game called hockey, the hockie.
items.cn: 英语中已知最早的 hockey 记录约在十六世纪二十年代，戈尔韦的一项法令禁止一种名为 hockey 的球棒运动。

items.en: A competing proposal links the word to Old Irish cadan, a ball or hurling ball; this is listed as uncertain, not settled fact.
items.cn: 另一种说法认为它源自古爱尔兰语 cadan（球、爱尔兰式曲棍球用球），此说仅属存疑假说。

items.en: Hockey becomes the general word for the grass game, later distinguished in Britain as field hockey.
items.cn: 十八至十九世纪，hockey 逐渐成为草地曲棍球的通称，后来在英国被区分为 field hockey。

items.en: In Canada the word attaches to the ice game, and in the United States it mainly names ice hockey.
items.cn: 十九世纪起，加拿大把这个词用于冰上比赛，美国则多指冰球。

note.en: Hockey is a ball game whose name is tied to its hooked stick; the spelling twin hock has nothing to do with it.
note.cn: hockey 是以弯头球棒命名的球类运动，拼写相近的 hock 与它并无关系。

entries.definition: the joint of a horse leg, or wine sold in pawn
entries.definitionCN: 马的后踝关节；典当葡萄酒，只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: the curved stick used in hockey
entries.definitionCN: 曲棍球棒，hockey 最常见的复合词

entries.definition: a person who plays hockey
entries.definitionCN: 曲棍球或冰球运动员

entries.definition: a hockey player, chiefly in Indian English
entries.definitionCN: 曲棍球运动员，主要见于印度英语

entries.definition: hockey played on ice with a puck
entries.definitionCN: 在冰面上用冰球进行的比赛

entries.definition: hockey played on grass or turf with a ball
entries.definitionCN: 在草地或人工草皮上用球进行的曲棍球

entries.definition: an Irish stick and ball game of great speed
entries.definitionCN: 爱尔兰式曲棍球，节奏极快

entries.definition: the hard flat disc used in ice hockey
entries.definitionCN: 冰球，冰球运动中被击打的扁圆盘

normalIntro.en: Hockey pictures a bent stick and a goal at each end, whether on grass or on ice.
normalIntro.cn: hockey 的画面是一根弯头球棒和两端的球门，无论在草地还是在冰上。

normal.en: The name comes from a hooked stick, so -ey with a curved shape in mind.
normal.cn: 名字源于弯钩状的球棒，记拼写时想象那根弯棍。

normal.en: Pair it: ice hockey on a frozen rink, field hockey on a green pitch.
normal.cn: 成对记：ice hockey 在冰场，field hockey 在草场。

normal.en: Hockey stick is its most common compound, like baseball bat for baseball.
normal.cn: hockey stick 是最常见的复合词，作用相当于棒球里的棒。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with hock, which means a horse joint or pawned wine.
normal.cn: 不要与 hock 混淆，后者指马的关节或典当的葡萄酒。

normal.en: British speakers say hockey for the grass game, North Americans say it for the ice game.
normal.cn: 英国人用 hockey 指草地曲棍球，北美人用它指冰球。

abstract.en: Picture two teams bending low, sticks tapping ice before the whistle.
abstract.cn: 想象两队球员弯下腰，哨响前球棒轻敲冰面。

abstract.en: Think of a shepherd leaning on a curved crook that became a sports stick.
abstract.cn: 想象牧羊人拄着一根弯钩棍，那根棍后来变成了运动球棒。

abstract.en: Imagine a locker room where the sticks stand in a row like tall bent walking canes.
abstract.cn: 想象更衣室里一排球棒立着，像一根根弯头手杖。

examples.en: She has played hockey since she was six years old.
examples.cn: 她从六岁起就开始打曲棍球。

examples.en: The ice hockey final went into extra minutes before a goal settled it.
examples.cn: 冰球决赛进入加时赛，最后一记进球才分出胜负。

examples.en: He left his hockey stick leaning against the goalpost.
examples.cn: 他把球棒靠在球门柱上就离开了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「猴球」——猴子抢球般满场追着弯棍乱跑，正是 hockey；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古法语 hoquet／hoket（弯头棍，词源存疑）→ 英语 hockey（一种用弯棍击球的运动，首见约十六世纪）→ 泛指草地曲棍球与冰球，核心义「用弯头球棒把球赶进球门」。

sensesIntro.en: Hockey first names the stick game itself, then covers the ice version in North America, and in casual use can point back at the stick.
sensesIntro.cn: hockey 先指用弯棍击球的运动本身，再指北美的冰上版本，口语里还能回指那根球棒。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a curved stick pushing a ball or puck toward a goal.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根弯头球棒把球推向球门。

branches.en: The stick game itself is the original and general sense.
branches.cn: 用球棒击球的运动本身是本源且通用的义项。

branches.en: The ice version is the North American extension of the same game.
branches.cn: 冰球版本是同一项运动在北美的发展。

branches.en: The gear sense reflects a casual return to the stick the name came from.
branches.cn: 球具义反映了口语回到命名源头的球棒。

branches.en: Field hockey and ice hockey share one name and one set of rules family.
branches.cn: 草地曲棍球与冰球共用一个名称和一套规则谱系。

branches.en: Ice hockey equipment such as the stick and puck is where the word is heard most often today.
branches.cn: 球棒与冰球等装备正是今天最常听到这个词的场合。

intro.en: Hockey has no productive prefix; its history is a short noun of a stick and a ball, later compounded with stick and player.
intro.cn: hockey 没有能产的前缀，其历史是一根弯棍与一个球构成的短名词，后来与 stick、player 组成复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin has no source word for hockey; the nearest classical item is the noun hocus, later the base of hoquet, a diminutive, and its origin remains disputed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中没有 hockey 的来源词，最接近的是名词 hocus（钩子），后来构成指小词 hoquet，其来源本身仍有争议。

items.example: Old French hoquet is the most commonly suggested source.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 hoquet 是最常被提到的来源词。

items.example: Hockey entered English around the sixteenth century.
items.exampleCN: hockey 约在十六世纪进入英语。

items.exampleCN: ice hockey 中的 ice 标明滑冰场地。

items.exampleCN: 复合词 hockey stick 指主要球具。

definition_zh: 吊起；升起；举起；将船升起；起重机；吊装设备
definition_en: to lift something heavy by means of ropes, a crane, or machinery, especially straight up; also the lifting device itself
core_image: 滑轮组把沉重的货物连同绳带一起直直吊离地面
scene: 码头上，工人开动吊机，把装满粮食的麻袋从船舱缓缓吊到甲板。The workers hoist the heavy sacks from the hold onto the deck.
sceneCN: 这里 hoist 是「吊起、升起」（第 1 个义项：借助绳索或机械把重物笔直提上去）；句意：工人们把沉重的麻袋从货舱吊到甲板上。画面重点：滑轮、绳带、缓缓升高的货物。

pos.zh: 吊起；升起；举起；升起（帆、旗）；将船升起
起重机；吊装设备；升降装置

hoist 加 -ing 作名词，指吊装、起吊作业

senses.title: To lift something heavy straight up
senses.definition: to raise something heavy by pulling on ropes or by using a crane or other machinery
senses.definitionCN: 用绳索拉动或借助起重机等机械把重物提起来
senses.example: Volunteers hoisted the crates onto the truck.
senses.exampleCN: 志愿者们把木箱吊上了卡车。
senses.why: The core image places ropes, pulleys and a load together, so the primary meaning is a weight rising under control.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象把绳索、滑轮和货物捆在一起，因此最基本的含义是重物在控制下垂直上升；动词义至今仍带「费力、需要工具」的味道。

senses.title: To raise a flag or a sail
senses.definition: to pull a flag or a sail up a pole or a mast so that it opens and shows
senses.definitionCN: 把旗帜或船帆沿旗杆、桅杆向上拉起，使其展开显现
senses.example: The ship hoisted its flag as it entered the harbour.
senses.exampleCN: 船驶入港口时升起了自己的旗帜。
senses.why: A flag is pulled up on a rope just as a load is, so the maritime lifting image passes straight into ceremonial flagraising.
senses.whyCN: 旗子也是用绳索拉上去的，和吊货用的是同一套动作，于是航海里的吊升动作自然延伸到升旗、升帆这类仪式性场合。

senses.title: To lift a person up
senses.definition: to lift a person up, often with effort or with help from others
senses.definitionCN: 把人举起来，通常费力或需他人协助
senses.example: The nurses hoisted him gently into the chair.
senses.exampleCN: 护士们轻轻地把他扶到椅子上。
senses.why: The object of hoisting need not be cargo, so putting a patient or a child into a chair keeps the same effortful lifting motion.
senses.whyCN: 被吊起的东西不必是货物，把人搀扶、抬到椅子上仍是同一个费力的上升动作，只是对象换了人，语气也更讲体谅。

senses.title: To raise something into the air
senses.definition: to lift an object high into the air, for example as a sign of victory
senses.definitionCN: 把物体高擎空中，例如作为胜利的表示
senses.example: The captain hoisted the cup above his head.
senses.exampleCN: 队长把奖杯高高举过头顶。
senses.why: Because the result of hoisting is something held high, the verb is used for the triumphant gesture of raising a trophy.
senses.whyCN: 吊升的结果就是东西被举到高处，所以这个动词也用来描述夺冠后把奖杯高高举起的庆祝手势。

senses.title: To lift a boat out of the water
senses.definition: to lift a boat out of the water, especially for repair or storage
senses.definitionCN: 把船从水中吊起，尤其为了修理或存放
senses.example: The yard hoists small boats for winter storage.
senses.exampleCN: 船厂把小船吊上岸过冬存放。
senses.why: Small craft are hauled up in slings exactly like freight on a dock, so boatlifting became a specialised hoisting sense.
senses.whyCN: 小艇是用吊带整艘吊起来的，和码头上吊货毫无二致，于是「把船吊出水面」成了这个动词在船厂里的专门义项。

senses.title: A machine for lifting
senses.definition: a device with ropes, chains and a pulley used to lift heavy loads
senses.definitionCN: 用绳索、链条和滑轮提起重物的装置
senses.example: The chain hoist creaked as the engine block rose.
senses.exampleCN: 发动机缸体升起时，链式起重机吱吱作响。
senses.why: The act and its instrument share one word, so the verb that once described the action became a noun naming the iron that does it.
senses.whyCN: 动作和工具共用一个词，原本描述动作的动词转成名词，用来指做这件事的那台铁家伙，这是英语里极常见的「动作转器具」。

senses.title: A lifting system in a building
senses.definition: a lifting mechanism or the shaft that serves it in a building
senses.definitionCN: 建筑物中的升降机械，以及为它服务的井道
senses.example: The hoistway houses the hoist that serves all floors.
senses.exampleCN: 井道里装着服务所有楼层的升降装置。
senses.why: Once the noun names any lifting gear, the word extends to the permanent machinery and shaft inside a building.
senses.whyCN: 当这个名词泛指各类起重设备之后，就自然延伸到建筑物里固定安装的升降机械和井道，成为工程用语。

intro.en: Hoist is usually traced to a nautical lifting word, probably of Low German origin, which entered English in the late sixteenth century.
intro.cn: hoist 一般被追溯到航海里的起吊用语，很可能源自低地德语，于十六世纪后期进入英语。

items.en: The ultimate origin is uncertain; most dictionaries point to a nautical term rather than a Latin verb.
items.cn: 最终来源不确定，多数词典认为它是航海术语，而不是直接从某个拉丁动词变来。

items.en: Compare Low German hissen, to haul up a sail, often given as the likely source.
items.cn: 可比较低地德语 hissen（把帆拉起来），一般认为这是最可能的来源。

items.en: Hoist is first recorded in English in the sixteenth century as a command to haul up a sail.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语里首次记录到 hoist，当时是水手拉起船帆的口令。

items.en: By the eighteenth century the verb covers general lifting with ropes and pulleys.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，这个动词已泛指用绳索和滑轮吊起重物。

items.en: The noun appears for lifting machinery as engineering and shipping expand.
items.cn: 随着工程与航运发展，作名词的 hoist 出现，指起重机械。

items.en: Modern English uses hoist for cranes, lifts, boatyards and figurative raising.
items.cn: 现代英语用它描述起重机、升降机、船厂作业以及比喻性的「高擎」。

note.en: Hoist belongs to the vocabulary of ropes and winches, close to haul, heave and the cranes that carry their names.
note.cn: hoist 属于绳索与绞车的词汇场，与 haul、heave 以及同样用作器械名的 crane 等词相邻。

normalIntro.en: Hoist is rope work: a load that rises because someone is pulling on a line.
normalIntro.cn: hoist 是绳索活：因为有绳子被拉动，重物才升了上去。

normal.en: To hoist a flag is to pull it up a pole.
normal.cn: hoist a flag 就是把旗子沿旗杆拉上去。

normal.en: Cargo is hoisted onto a ship by a crane.
normal.cn: 货物由起重机吊上船。

normal.en: A chain hoist is a lifting machine with a chain, not a rope.
normal.cn: chain hoist 是用链条传动的起重装置。

normal.en: Nurses hoist a patient into a chair, while workers hoist a crate onto a truck.
normal.cn: 护士把病人扶上椅子，工人把木箱吊上卡车，用法相同。

normal.en: The noun and the verb share one spelling, so the hoist is the thing that hoists.
normal.cn: 名词和动词同形，因此「吊起」的那台机器也叫 hoist。

abstract.en: Picture a rope creaking over a pulley as a crate rises past a ship rail.
abstract.cn: 想象绳索在滑轮上吱吱作响，木箱贴着船舷升过栏杆。

abstract.en: See a flag flapping open the moment it reaches the top of the mast.
abstract.cn: 想象旗帜升到桅杆顶端的一刹那迎风展开。

abstract.en: Feel the strain of lifting a heavy bag over a high wall with a partner.
abstract.cn: 体会两人合力把一只沉重的袋子抬过高墙时的那种吃力。

examples.cn: 工人们用小吊车把钢梁吊上了屋顶。

examples.en: Every morning the pupils hoist the flag in the school yard.
examples.cn: 每天早晨，学生们在校园里升旗。

examples.en: The old chain hoist in the garage is heavier than the engine it lifts.

dict_mnemonic.text: 「好丝」——好结实的丝绳，才能把重物吊起来；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 来源一般认为与低地德语 hissen（拉起船帆）有关，经航海用语进入英语；核心义「沿绳索把重物向上吊起」，与拉丁语并无直接派生关系。

sensesIntro.en: Hoist begins as a sailor lifting a sail, then widens to cargo, flags, people and trophies, and finally names the machine that does the lifting.
sensesIntro.cn: hoist 从水手拉起船帆开始，扩展到货物、旗帜、人与奖杯，最后还用来命名做这件事的机械。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a load rising straight up on a rope.
core.cn: 核心意象：重物被绳索直直吊起。

branches.en: General lifting of heavy goods is the original verbal sense.
branches.cn: 吊起沉重货物是最早的动词义项。

branches.en: Raising a flag or sail keeps the maritime image.
branches.cn: 升帆升旗保留了航海画面。

branches.en: People and trophies are raised with the same upward effort.
branches.cn: 抬人与举杯用的是同一种向上用力。

branches.en: Lifting boats out of water is the shipyard sense.
branches.cn: 把船吊出水面是船厂的专门义项。

branches.en: The action turns into the noun for the machinery itself.
branches.cn: 动作转为名词，指起重与升降设备本身。

intro.en: Hoist is a short native-looking word with no Latin parts; its family grows with -er, -ing and compounding.
intro.cn: hoist 词形短，看不出拉丁构件，它的家族靠 -er、-ing 与复合构词扩展。

latinIntro.en: There is no secure Latin ancestor for hoist, so the Latin entries here are those of a closely related word family used for comparison.
latinIntro.cn: hoist 没有可靠的拉丁语祖先，这里列出的是对照用的相关词族拉丁构件，仅作构词参考。

definition_zh: 整体的；全面的；整体观的
definition_en: treating a system, person, or subject as a complete whole rather than as a set of separate parts
core_image: 一只手同时托起整个拼图，而不是只盯着一块拼片
scene: 医生没有只查一种症状，而是把病人的饮食、睡眠和家庭压力放在一起考虑。She takes a holistic view of her patients, looking at body and mind together.
sceneCN: 这里 holistic 是「整体的、全面的」（第 1 个义项：把对象看作完整的整体，而不是把各部分拆开来看）；句意：她以整体的眼光看待病人，把身体与心理放在一起考虑。

pos.zh: 整体的；全面的；整体观的

derivatives.zh: 整体论；整体主义，来自希腊语 holos（整个）加名词后缀 -ism
整体论者，holism 去掉 -ism 后加 -ist
holistic 加副词后缀 -ally，义为「从整体上」

senses.title: Looking at the whole rather than the parts
senses.definition: treating something as a complete whole, so that the parts are understood through their relations to one another
senses.definitionCN: 把事物视为一个完整的整体，通过各部分之间的相互关联来理解它们
senses.example: The report takes a holistic view of city transport.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告从整体上考察城市交通。
senses.why: The Greek root holos means whole, so the adjective begins by naming any method that starts from the whole and moves to the parts.
senses.whyCN: 希腊词根 holos 意为「整个」，所以这个形容词首先指从整体出发、再看部分的方法。

senses.title: Caring for the whole person
senses.definition: attending to a person as a whole, so that physical, mental, and social needs are considered together
senses.definitionCN: 把人当作一个整体来照料，使身体、心理和社会方面的需要一并得到考虑
senses.example: The clinic offers holistic care for older patients.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所对老年病人提供整体照护。
senses.why: Medicine splits a person into parts, so the opposing image naturally turns the word into a label for care that refuses to split people up.
senses.whyCN: 现代医学常把人拆成各个器官，与之相反的画面就让这个词成了「不把人拆开」的医疗照护名称。

senses.title: Describing the whole of something
senses.definition: covering all aspects of a subject rather than one part of it
senses.definitionCN: 涵盖一个问题的各个方面，而非只涉及一部分
senses.example: The council needs a holistic assessment of the risks.
senses.exampleCN: 议会需要对风险作一次综合评估。
senses.why: Once whole is part of its meaning, the adjective can simply describe any picture or assessment that covers everything at stake.
senses.whyCN: 既然「整个」已是它的词义，这个形容词就可以直接描述任何涵盖全部相关方面的图景或评估。

senses.title: Related to the theory of holism
senses.definition: of or holding the theory that wholes have properties that their parts do not
senses.definitionCN: 属于或秉持「整体具有其部分所不具备的性质」这一理论的
senses.example: Holistic theories in biology insist that systems cannot be reduced to parts.
senses.exampleCN: 生物学的整体论主张系统不能被还原为各个部分。
senses.why: The philosophical term holism gave the adjective a technical sense in which the existence of the whole is itself an argument.
senses.whyCN: 哲学上的整体论给了这个形容词一个专业含义，此时「整体的存在」本身就成了一种论证。

senses.title: Explaining by whole systems
senses.definition: explaining behaviour by the working of a whole system rather than by single units
senses.definitionCN: 用整个系统的运作来解释行为，而不是归因于单个单元
senses.example: Ecologists prefer holistic explanations to single causes.
senses.exampleCN: 生态学家偏爱系统性的解释，而不求单一原因。
senses.why: Systems research takes whole networks as its unit of study, so the word acquired a scientific sense in which parts are effects, not causes.
senses.whyCN: 系统研究把整个网络当作研究单位，于是这个词在科学领域获得新义：起作用的是整体，部分只是结果。

intro.en: Holistic is a twentieth century coinage built on holism, which the statesman Jan Smuts formed in the nineteen twenties from Greek holos, whole.
intro.cn: holistic 是二十世纪的造词，建立在 holism 之上；holism 由政治人物扬·史末资在二十年代用希腊语 holos（整个）造成。

items.en: Holos means whole, entire and complete.
items.cn: 希腊语 holos 意为整个的、全部的、完整的。

items.en: Jan Smuts coins holism in his book Holism and Evolution.
items.cn: 一九二六年，扬·史末资在《整体论与进化》一书中造出 holism 一词。

items.en: Holistic appears in Philosophy and Scientific Method, a book of essays published in 1922.
items.cn: holistic 首次见于一九二二年出版的论文集《哲学与科学方法》。

items.en: The adjective spreads from philosophy and biology into medicine.
items.cn: 这个形容词从哲学与生物学扩展到医学领域。

items.en: Holistic care, holistic education and holistic approach become common phrase patterns.
items.cn: 二十世纪后期，整体照护、整体教育与整体方法成为常见搭配。

items.en: In modern English the word is used widely for all aspects of a system.
items.cn: 现代英语中，这个词广泛用于指一个系统的方方面面。

note.en: Holistic sits between the noun holism and its opposite atomistic, and is often confused with holy and with wholesome.
note.cn: holistic 位于名词 holism 与它的对立说法 atomistic 之间，常与 holy、wholesome 混淆。

entries.definition: in a way that treats something as a whole
entries.definitionCN: holistic 加 -ally 的副词形式，义为「从整体上」

entries.definition: the theory that wholes are more than their parts
entries.definitionCN: 整体论；holistic 的名词基础
